Industry observers note that homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S. Entressangle/E. Daynes/SPL.

In a recent development, fossil teeth suggest that Homo erectus thrived in dense rainforests in southern China as recently as 180,000 years ago. Researchers had thought that these ancient hominins had been limited to savannahs and open woodlands, states Kira Westaway, a geochronologist and a co-author of two newly introduced studies. “This is a really major deal, because we thought Homo sapiens were the only species that had the skill set to survive in really challenging rainforest environments.”.

Reference: Nature paper 1 & paper 2.

Industry observers note that artificial-intelligence giant Anthropic has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November. The firm — now valued at a staggering US$1.5 trillion — has major ambitions in science. It made waves earlier this year when it reported that its model Claude had made several major mathematics breakthroughs. The manufacturer also debuted their first ‘wet’ laboratory for life sciences research and has declared aims to “substantially” scale up its work in AI-enabled drug discovery. Pitched as a company that prioritizes AI safety, some researchers question whether an IPO — and the accompanying investor demands — might disrupt some of Anthropic’s safety commitments.

In a recent development, roughly 180 million people could be carrying a previously unknown type of giant virus in their guts. Researchers found DNA from these ‘egoviruses’ in gut samples from people, buffalo, goats, chickens, deer and pigs. Six clades were unique to people, one of which is estimated to be present in roughly 1% of the population. Microbiologists say that egoviruses could be the missing link between giant viruses that infect single-celled organisms and distantly related poxviruses, such as those that cause smallpox and mpox, which can infect people and animals directly.

Here in Washington DC, tens of thousands of researchers have gathered for the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting — a showcase for everything from neural implants to memory research.

Industry observers note that but when I asked a panel of leaders at the US National Institutes of Health what in neuroscience remains underappreciated, several pointed to the brain’s relationship with the rest of the body. Nora Volkow, director of the National Institute on Drug Abuse, lamented the lack of research into brain metabolism — a blind spot exposed by the surprising neurological effects of GLP-1 drugs.

Amy Bany Adams, acting director of the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, offered a reminder of how much remains to be discovered. Of the glymphatic system, the brain’s waste-clearance network, she remarked: “We didn’t even know it existed when I was in graduate school.” I’m leaving with a longer list of questions about what else we’ve been overlooking.

Neuroscientists are uncovering how the brain orchestrates a tailored mixture of symptoms in response to either a bacterial or viral infection. Presenting at the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting on 15 November, researchers suggested that the brain decodes the type of pathogen that has invaded, accesses memories of past bouts of illness and can even mobilize immune defences at the sight of a sick person. The unpublished findings challenge the long-held view that neurological responses to infection are a one-size-fits-all response to inflammation.

Artificial-intelligence governance requires more than companies’ oversight of their models — it requires “a system of accountability” that works like a national constitution, argues legal scholar Cindy Skach. Firms should be held legally liable when individuals are affected by AI actions that infringe on their fundamental rights, Skach suggests. She proposes ‘human dignity’ as the most crucial value for the system to uphold. When a person’s dignity is violated — by an AI-generated deepfake or by a chatbot that treats a distressed user as just another interaction — they could petition a court directly to hold the perpetrator accountable.

Do you find networking a nightmare? Three experts share — in the form of short videos — how to grasp the nettle. They suggest thinking about networking as a professional skill that can be learnt and developed, considering arriving early for events and not worrying about volume. One high-quality connection and follow-up conversation is worth more than 100 business cards, says public-speaking coach Susie Ashfield.

Recent findings suggest that in the second episode of Nature Podcast’s climate miniseries, host Nick Petrić Howe hears from scientists about what humanity can actually do to stop the runaway train of rising temperatures. The rise of renewable-energy technologies is already making a dent in greenhouse-gas emissions, experts say. But creating meat alternatives and a move away from an economic system that incentivizes ‘growth at any cost’ could help to really shift the dial.

Nature Podcast | 45 min listen or read the transcript.

Vertebrate palaeontologist Aldo Benites-Palomino explains why the extinct ancient whale — which evolved extreme facial asymmetry to to make space in its head for echolocation and sound production organs — was named with a Peruvian word for “anything that is flashy, over-the-top, bizarre, extravagant or difficult to categorize aesthetically”. (Discover | 7 min read).

Reference: Communications Biology paper.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03797-3.

Today I’m considering buying a prickly pear cactus (Opuntia) in case of a power cut. Researchers have found that the plants’ unusual method of photosynthesis can be harnessed to generate a small amount of electricity, with around eight prickly pears together generating nearly three times the voltage of a standard AA battery.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 06:20 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 06:30 EST, 21 November 2026.

The goalkeeper involved in the collision that killed Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel has been seen in public for the first time since the tragic accident.

During a match earlier this month, Andorra keeper Jesus Owono came flying out of his goal and wiped out Tenerife star de Miguel with a high challenge which resulted in the striker being admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

De Miguel's passing shocked the footballing world and Owono was subsequently given a 12-match ban by authorities.

Both sides have been back in action since the tragedy, but on Friday, Andorra hosted Leganes at their Estadi de la FAF.

That was their first home game since de Miguel's passing, and they made sure to pay a moving tribute to him on the night.

Before the match, the players went onto the pitch wearing shirts with his name and number on them and they carried out a bouquet of white flowers.

Andorra keeper Jesus Owono was seen in public for the first time since Jesus de Miguel's tragic death as he attended a tribute to the former Tenerife star.

Before Andorra's game with Legannes, several tributes were paid, including a minute's silence.

A minute's silence was also held before the game, while those in attendance applauded during the ninth minute of the match, the shirt number worn by de Miguel at Tenerife.

The most striking part of the evening though was Owono's attendance in the stands.

The goalkeeper has stayed away from the public eye since de Miguel's death, after which he was subjected to chants of 'murderer', but he wanted to attend the tribute at his club's home ground.

Owono was wearing a black coat and hat as he stood next to team-mates who weren't involved in the matchday squad.

Despite receiving the support of the crowd and his team-mates, local reports stated Owono cut a downcast figure and that he was seen praying immediately after the minute's silence.

Owono's desire to attend the tribute came after he had also asked to meet de Miguel's family, something he hopes to do one day.

Meanwhile, Tenerife returned to action last week against AD Ceuta CF in a match that was also filled with tributes.

Players provided a floral tribute as they arrived for the match, and gathered outside gate nine of the Heliodoro Rodríguez Lopez Stadium – another nod to de Miguel's shirt number.

Grief-stricken Tenerife stars then took to the field carrying a bouquet of flowers, and placed it at the scene of the tragedy.

Both sets of players and fans then observed a minute's silence in memory of de Miguel before the game kicked off.

The game was then brought to a pause in the ninth minute, so the players could pay another tribute.

Fans inside the stadium unveiled a tifo which read: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternal blanquiazul', which translates to: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally white and blue.'.

Recent findings suggest that other fans held up white and blue cards beside the tifo, with others in the ground applauding. When Tenerife scored, de Miguel's shirt was held in the air.

After the game, which Tenerife won 2-0, both teams gathered in the centre circle to place de Miguel's shirt on a bouquet of flowers, and the fans applauded to bring an end to an emotional day.

Owono was watching the game from the stands as he stood next to some of his team-mates.

Tenerife returned to action last week and paid several tributes to their former star de Miguel.

The tragedy occurred as the game between Tenerife and Andorra entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when de Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for his side in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, de Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Owono was given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

Owono's 12-match ban is at the moment in effect, yet his manager Carles Manso hinted that he may never play again.

He remarked: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that (he will do so).'.

It has been revealed that while no one has officially confirmed that Mauricio Pochettino is departing the United States men's national team for Manchester United after Michael Carrick's sacking, the faces of Sebastian Berhalter and Folarin Balogun remarked everything that you needed to know at media availability on Thursday ahead of their Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals match with Haiti. When asked about what he wanted to see, Balogun was succinct, saying, "If I had a vote, I would like to keep things the way they are.".

He continued, saying, "I think things have been working well; we have a clear sense of identity, we have a clear playing style, and whenever you have a top coach, you'd want him to stay, as it's a no-brainer, so I think for us it's no different.".

It's hard not to feel for Balogun after he became the story of the World Cup for the wrong reasons, with his red card rescinded before he played against Belgium in the round of 16, where the USMNT suffered a 4-1 loss, crashing out of the tournament. Then things went from bad to worse when his move to Everton was called off due to a change in contract terms, and now he is struggling for playing time at Monaco. While he still looks to leave the French club in January, the national team camp was supposed to be an escape, but instead it has become another uncertain period as Pochettino's days come to an end. Berhalter confirmed that the team hasn't officially heard anything, but that their focus is still on the game at hand.

"We're focused on going against Haiti twice; they're a good team. You saw at the World Cup, they surprised people, so that's our main focus, and I think the group is ready to play these games," Berhalter mentioned.

According to recent reports, berhalter made his national team debut under Pochettino and hasn't looked back, securing 22 caps for the team and making it hard for the Argentine to decide how he should set up the midfield. Because of that, it's hard not to be reflective in uncertain times like these.

"Personally, on the field and off the field, he's done a lot for me, and from day one he's always believed in me. Before I set foot on the field, I think about the way I play and the way that I try to carry myself," Berhalter said. "He just said it doesn't matter what you're doing on the field; these are already the right things. And to be honest, I can't thank him enough, and regardless if he's coach, not the coach and, I say it every time that he's meant so much to me. And he's helped me develop as a player and as a person, and as a player, that's all you can ask for: to have that trust and have that belief in you. And for me, it's easy to go out there and just do my job so, he's meant a good deal to me for sure.".

This is all tough to manage while having games to play. Sure, players will say they're going to be professionals, and these are people who have dealt with stress and needed to maintain that professionalism while doing so, but from a human perspective, it's a well-liked coach leaving on short notice. Even if people anticipated that Pochettino might not make it through to the 2030 World Cup and his departure was a sign that a coach who has done well at the helm was leaving, that doesn't make it any easier on the players. If they go ahead promptly against Haiti on Saturday, they could turn the match into a celebration of what has been so great while playing for Pochettino, but going behind can have a cascading impact where doubt starts to creep in. It's something that the USMNT will need to avoid, even if the future is bright for this squad, no matter who is coaching them.

In a recent development, pochettino helped raise the standard, and with young players like Cavan Sullivan, Adri Mehmeti, Matias Albert, Neil Pierre and Julian Hall, the future is already here, and no one can feel complacent about their spots. These are things that the newly introduced coach can bring in, and Pochettino's leadership can set a new standard of what to look for.

Industry observers note that "Yeah, I think the benefit and the blessing when you have a great coach is you know the standard," Balogun mentioned. "I think Poch definitely raised the standard since he's been in charge. I think you guys have seen that, just the intensity of training, how we approach games, he's changed our way of thinking as players, from calling the friendlies that we have in certain camps official games, not official games. He wants us to just be of a mindset to go out there and win.".

Recent findings suggest that "He's laid the foundation, and I think we, as players, have that ownership to not just do that because Poch was in charge; I think we have the ownership as players to carry that out because we know the standard," he continued. "So yeah, I think that's the benefit of having a top coach, and I'm sure you know whether he's here or not, the US will look to replace him with another top coach.".

According to recent reports, who succeeds Pochettino will be vital, but what the players have learned from his time will be invaluable, so the standard can't slip from here. As Balogun stated, it's time to take ownership of their own future because while the coaches may change, the players tasked with leading this team back to the top of Concacaf are already here and understand the task at hand.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future as reports emerged of other extramarital affairs — this time with employees.
  • In a statement issued on Thursday, the world's most valuable chip supplier said Huang was resigning as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately.
  • The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future as reports emerged of other extramarital affairs — this time with employees.

In a statement issued on Thursday, the world's most valuable chip supplier said Huang was resigning as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately.

The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO.

Under Nvidia's bylaws, Huang can be removed "with or without cause" by a majority vote of its 11 directors.

The Newly introduced York Times first reported that the 63-year-old Huang had an affair with a senior Nvidia executive who reported directly to him.

Later Thursday, Reuters news agency alleged an intimate relationship between Huang and a second employee, citing unidentified sources.

In a recent development, those revelations emerged just three days after Huang admitted a relationship with a Chinese woman, whom United States intelligence agencies believe was spying for China. The woman, Alice Huang — no relation — is a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm that runs artificial intelligence (AI) data centers across Southeast Asia and is a major client of Nvidia.

The US government is investigating the startup on suspicion that it secretly sent some of its Nvidia chips to China, violating Washington's curbs on high-end semiconductors.

Those advanced Nvidia processors ‌are ​used to train and run the large AI models behind chatbots and other generative AI products.

Recent findings suggest that megaspeed denies the allegations and on Thursday pledged to cooperate with US investigators. Huang, the alleged spy, has been barred from entering Singapore and Taiwan — a key chipmaking island.

While Nvidia's board backed its CEO after the first scandal emerged, market watchers believe the second caused too much reputational damage to one of the world's top three companies by market value.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Huang doesn't believe in formal succession planning, so with little notice, Nvidia appointed CFO Kress as interim CEO.

Bloomberg reported Wednesday that Nvidia’s board is working with advisers to identify potential permanent successors.

It has been revealed that kress, other senior Nvidia executives and members of Huang's own family have been mooted as replacements. The family members include his daughter Madison, a senior director of product marketing, and his son Spencer, who right now works in the firm's robotics division.

Rumors also abound over a longer-term solution. On India's CNBC-TV18, Jeffrey Sonnenfeld from the Yale School of Management floated former Apple CEO Tim Cook and ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt.

US President Donald Trump also backed Cook on social media, writing: "A Legend replaces a Legend.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The scandals have certainly hit Nvidia's market value. Since the first extramarital affair emerged on Sunday, the chipmaker's market capitalization has fallen by well over $600 billion to $4.2 trillion.

Industry observers note that nvidia shares were down more than 9% in premarket trading Thursday, after dropping by 10% earlier this week. Some analysts expect the stock price to struggle in the short term.

Nvidia stock hit all-time highs just a month ago as US technology giants continued to announce billions in spending on AI infrastructure.

Demand for Nvidia's advanced chips is so high, however, that many market analysts expect little impact on near-term sales.

"While Jensen [Huang] is the heart and lungs of the Nvidia story…the manufacturer and its leading-edge GPU technology will go on and [his departure] does not change the entrenched position Nvidia has in the AI Revolution chip arms race," said Dan Ives, a partner, senior managing director and tech analyst at Yorkville Ives, a US-based merchant bank.

Analysts see the biggest long-term risk in strategy and execution. After all, Huang was the leader who picked which ideas Nvidia should bet heavily on and got the whole company behind them.

His sudden exit is also seen as highly disruptive to the chip designer's strong relationships with AI hyperscalers, Taiwanese chip producer TSMC and foreign governments — especially China.

Huang was Nvidia's main lobbyist on US chip export rules and persuaded US President Donald Trump to ease some curbs on China last year.

Huang is often called a rockstar CEO for his leather jackets instead of suits.

Like Elon Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, he was also seen as a key-person risk as Nvidia’s public image, strategic direction and technical decisions became closely tied to him.

Huang steered the manufacturer for more than three decades and was also respected for his hands-on involvement in product architecture and engineering decisions.

He also insisted on a flat management structure, with around 60 executives reporting directly to him.

Huang has run the firm so tightly around his own technical judgment and product decisions that investors may have little sense of how it would function without him.

Recent findings suggest that at the same time, Nvidia is no longer the startup Huang founded in 1993. The organization has built deep expertise in chip design and software, creating a durable moat that helps protect its huge profits, which topped $120.1 billion last year.

Some analysts argue that its central role in the AI hardware buildout makes it less dependent on Huang’s day-to-day input.

China is rapidly playing catch-up with the US in the global race for AI dominance.

While Chinese AI models have lagged behind the likes of ChatGPT and Claude, recent updates from DeepSeek, Alibaba and Moonshot have closed much of the gap on benchmark tests and often beat US rivals on cost and speed.

Beijing is also investing heavily in domestic chips and data centers to reduce reliance on US hardware.

The US has curbed exports to China of Nvidia's most advanced AI chips.

However, this move has only slowed the pace of China's AI ambitions.

Reuters reported Thursday that Chinese AI firms are now trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at data centers outside China, amid fears the US could further tighten restrictions on advanced chips.

Also Thursday, Beijing accused the US of using the Nvidia spying claims as a pretext to impose a technological "blockade" on China.

The concern is likely to dominate talks next week between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC gathering in Shenzhen in southern China.

Unai Emery has managed more than 1,100 matches but will never forget the drama of “La Remontada” as he returns to the scene on Tuesday night.

Recent findings suggest that emery is back at the Nou Camp in the Champions League for the first time since one of the most epic games in the history of the competition. While in charge of Paris St-Germain nine years ago, Emery took his team to Barcelona with a 4-0 lead from the round-of-16 first leg. Yet he was left stunned as Barcelona recovered to win the rematch 6-1, with three goals in the final seven minutes and the winner proving hugely controversial.

Sergi Roberto’s goal five minutes into added time caused a massive backlash as PSG claimed it was offside, with Emery claiming on Monday that the match revealed that VAR was “necessary”.

It has been revealed that aston Villa have made the trip over to Spain to take on Barcelona in the Champions League on matchday four. These teams last met all the way back in 1983, when they met in the European Super Cup. Barcelona won the first leg 1-0 at home before Aston Villa claimed a 3-0 victory at Villa Park, meaning Villa progressed 3-1 on aggregate.

It has been revealed that aston Villa have made the perfect start to their Champions League campaign, winning all three games, beating Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking, scoring 12 goals in the process. Unai Emery’s side drew 1-1 at home against Fulham in the league on Saturday. Emery, who celebrates his 55th birthday today, has a very dismal record against Barcelona, taking just three wins from 30 matches. His last Champions League game at the Nou Camp was infamous as his PSG side lost 6-1 to go out in the last 16 back in 2017 despite winning the first leg of that tie 4-0.

“In 1982, Villa won the European Cup, and we like to think about playing in this competition again and trying to repeat that success,” Emery said. “Barcelona are favourites for what they have done in the last ten years; now they need to prove why they are favourites.

It has been revealed that “[Barcelona] have [Lamine] Yamal. He is a special player. You can see in him as a player who could end up being the best. He needs a few things but he could end up being a great player. Rodri gives personality to the team. They have [Anthony] Gordon giving them speed and hard work. They have Pedri or Fermin [Lopez] as offensive midfielders.”.

Barcelona started strongly in the Champions League, winning their first two games, but lost 4-2 at defending champions PSG last time out. They warmed up for this match with an emphatic 6-1 win over Alaves in La Liga on Saturday. That victory gives them a two-point lead at the summit of La Liga.

“We know that at this level, anything can happen,” Barcelona boss Hansi Flick said. “Against Real Madrid, the result could have been different. These are special matches, but we are staying confident. It is normal to focus more on our last two defeats, but I have confidence in my team, which demonstrated it again on Saturday. Now, we are focused on the Champions League, with the goal of finishing in the top eight. For me, he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world and he has reaped extraordinary successes. His team’s style of play is clear and very well organised. Just look at how they execute set pieces; it is something impressive. Their confidence in themselves is unmatched. It will be a tough match against a great team and a great coach.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that espanyol beat Athletic Club 1-0 in Bilbao through a Roberto Fernández goal. The result extends a strong run since Manolo González left and leaves Athletic seventh after a home defeat in which they dominated the statistics.

A crowd of 46,107 was at San Mamés on Friday 20 November 2026. The fixture opened Matchday 13 of LaLiga EA Sports.

The win was Eder Sarabia’s first in charge of Espanyol. The club have now taken seven of the nine points available since González left, according to EFE. Espanyol named Sarabia head coach on 28 October 2026, on a contract that runs until 2028.

His appointment followed a 4-3 Copa del Rey defeat at Sestao River. A 1-0 win over Villarreal, a 0-0 draw with Deportivo La Coruna and Friday’s victory in Bilbao make up Espanyol’s results since González’s exit. Their goal difference now stands at zero.

Recent findings suggest that the first half ended goalless. Tyrhys Dolan replaced Pere Milla in the 57th minute. Sarabia also sent on Gabriel Moscardó and Javi Hernández in the 65th minute.

Industry observers note that A minute later, Dolan set up Fernández for the winner. It was the striker’s sixth league goal of the season, putting him eighth in the LaLiga scoring list. He finished with 3 shots and a rating of 7.92.

According to recent reports, sarabia then brought on Unai Núñez and Javi Puado in the 84th minute to protect the lead. Clemens Riedel was booked in the third minute of stoppage time, Espanyol’s only card of the night.

Industry observers note that in front of goalkeeper Ángel Fortuño, who kept a clean sheet, defender O. El Hilali was rated 7.16.

According to recent reports, the result gave Espanyol a third successive league win over Athletic. They won 2-0 at home on 13 May 2026 and 2-1 at San Mamés on 22 December 2025.

It has been revealed that athletic controlled most of the statistics. They had 58% of possession and 9 corners to Espanyol’s 2. On target, the hosts had 6 efforts and the visitors 3.

Edin Terzić moved away from the 4-4-2 he had used in previous matches to fit Oihan Sancet into a 4-2-3-1. The change did not produce more attacking threat. Deia judged this to be Athletic’s worst performance at San Mamés since Terzić took charge.

Nico Williams had 5 shots and 3 key passes. Iñigo Ruiz de Galarreta also created 3 chances in 29 minutes on the pitch. Athletic collected three yellow cards, for Iñaki Williams, Ruiz de Galarreta and Yeray Álvarez.

Athletic fall to defeat at San Mames.#AthleticEspanyol #AthleticClub 🦁 pic.twitter.com/tRnTpjuX14.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The last time FC Barcelona lost a match in the UEFA Women's Champions League was during the 2024-25 UWCL final in Lisbon. Arsenal walked off in Lisbon, Portugal, as Champions League winners and lifted the trophy as Europe's best. On Thursday, Arsenal went into Camp Nou and walked away with a different kind of tournament upset but valuable for their momentum: a 1-1 draw against the current title holders, Barcelona.

According to recent reports, barca's league phase win streak is snapped at three, and Arsenal's efforts lift them inside the top four for the league phase standings. Frida Maanum's goal put the Gunners on the board, while Caroline Graham Hansen equalized for Barcelona. After the final whistle, Arsenal left with the better momentum as matchday five approaches on Nov. 18.

Here's how Arsenal stole the point and Barcelona leveled:.

In a recent development, the visiting side took the game to Barcelona early. Immediately setting the tempo, disrupting the home side's rhythm and turning that into an early chance from Alessia Russo. The moment immediately opened the game up, and Barcelona quickly operated in the final third to record dangerous shots of their own during the opening ten minutes of the match.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal's Misa Rodriguez stepped up to stop shots, made her shape bigger, and even used her face to block Barcelona's peppering of attempts on target. The team effort to shut out Barcelona in the opening half was an everybody-on-the-pitch approach, with U.S. women's national team defender Emily Fox making a goalkeeping save as well.

WHATEVER IT TAKES 😤Emily Fox and Misa Rodríguez put their bodies on the line for Arsenal 💪Stream every UEFA Women’s Champions League game on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/JqjVCGd8RI.

"I found it hard. I mean, Barcelona is such a good team. Playing them at the Camp Nou, no, is a dream. But the match was a lot of running, a lot of defensive effort from the whole team, top to bottom, but we got the tie," Fox mentioned after the game.

Recent findings suggest that "I think in the first half, their adjustment, they started to have more rotations out. So I think for us, not being stagnant and really being aggressive and trying our best to keep them out of the pockets and outside the center of the field, that was a big thing that we talked about. And then from the first half, first on corners and first on blocking shots," Fox explained.

Sometimes the defensive efforts lead to transitional moments of play, and Arsenal's shift in personnel also helped change things in the game.

The group were motivated by the significant match-up, and got on the scoreboard within the opening 25 minutes of the game. Mariona Caldentey is out with injury, and Frida Maanum's return to the lineup was an immediate game changer. Russo is the club's leading goalscorer this season; she scored a hat-trick against Benfica and is now the leading English goalscorer in the competition's history.

But her efforts against Barcelona helped set up Maanum's opening goal. It was a reminder that the Gunners do have other options even when their main outlet is in top form, and the group carried a narrow one-goal lead into halftime.

FRIDA MAANUM STUNS THE CAMP NOU INTO SILENCE 🤐Arsenal are ahead in Barcelona completely against the run of play 😳Stream every UEFA Women’s Champions League game on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/x3AQAVzm7o.

"I think, you know, the last time we played them, we had some amazing memories, and we knew for them, coming to their place, it was going to be a hard game, and they probably saw it as a rematch, as did we," Fox stated.

"So, I think having confidence in our game plan and each other, knowing that we were going to work for each other no matter what, no matter [the] mistakes, what have you, and during halftime, we just talked about keep doing what we're doing, keep giving them a hard time, keep being aggressive, physical, bumping, and blocking them. And we have 45 minutes to go.".

It has been revealed that the second half was as energetic as the opening 45 minutes, and Barcelona increased the urgency even with some players unavailable due to injury. The roster flexed their depth with no Vicky Lopez, Kerolin, or Kika Nazareth, and with Aitana Bonmati only available off the bench.

With her left leg wrapped in medical tape, Caroline Graham Hansen scored the equalizer just before the hour mark.

CAROLINE GRAHAM HANSEN’S ROCKET HAS CAMP NOU ON THEIR FEET AT 1-1 🚀Stream every UEFA Women’s Champions League game on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/0lZEfWJg8f.

Recent findings suggest that "Happy that it's over. But yeah, I'm tired," Graham Hansen joked after the game.

"No,  it was a game that I feel like we deserve to win. But on the other hand, we also have to give credit to Arsenal. Like, they were there in the last moment to block a lot of shots. Did a good job to be there with us all the way, and to try to make it difficult for us to score. But yeah, on any other given day, I think it's crazy that we don't score more goals on the chances we created today," she mentioned.

Industry observers note that barcelona's 24 shots and seven attempts on target essentially tripled Arsenal's shot total (seven). The other silver lining for the group, other than salvaging a point, is the efforts of their depth players to keep creating in the game.

Industry observers note that "I'm not surprised. I've seen them for a couple of years now, and it was just a matter of time; it was their time to step forward. It was this season, and I was very sure that it would be a matter of confidence," Graham Hansen remarked about her teammates stepping up.

Recent findings suggest that "And now, when you play more, you get more confidence, and they also take the opportunities they get and show that they're ready, they want to play, and because the quality we knew was there, so I'm not surprised, and I'm just happy for them that they are able to keep showing themselves in the big moments. Because that's what we need, and that's also what they need to keep having the confidence high for the rest of the season.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United could be about to make a shock sale, which would divide the fans.

The business would represent the first major transfer market activity of fresh manager Mauricio Pochettino, who arrived at Manchester United this week after two years in charge of the United States men's national team.

With the Red Devils languishing in the relegation zone, it's accepted that the club will have to recruit to turn fortunes around – but there may well be a clearout, too, of underperformers.

With many of the squad that Pochettino has inherited coming under fire this season, there could be major exits in the upcoming January transfer window.

32-year-old club captain Bruno Fernandes' future is uncertain, World Cup winner Lisandro Martinez has hit out at directors behind the scenes and Marcus Rashford has been linked with a permanent departure after Michael Carrick reintegrated him at Carrington – but now another name has emerged as a move that should split the fanbase.

Sport Witness have relayed a report from Turkish outlet Sabah on Amad Diallo's future, with Besiktas keen on signing the wide man.

Both Vaclav Cerny and Ernest Poku have struggled for the Black Eagles, who are apparently looking to the Premier League for a new option on the right flank.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

The report mentions that Aston Villa were interested in the Ivorian over the summer, but with Bryan Mbeumo the first choice on the right wing – and only filling in up front in the absence of Benjamin Sesko – Amad's role is a little unclear in the squad.

Having made just four senior appearances at Atalanta, Amad joined United in 2021 in a late-window move before heading on loan to Rangers and Sunderland to develop further.

He returned for the 2023/24 season – getting sent off against Liverpool in March 2024 for a second yellow card when he removed his shirt in celebration of scoring the winner – but after establishing himself as a linchpin of Ruben Amorim's back three system, the 24-year-old has just two assists since the Portuguese was relieved of duties in the dugout, with his last goal coming almost a year ago.

Despite this, United fans would likely be torn on his exit: while Amad isn't in good form and hasn't shown that he can become a world-beater by any stretch, he is certainly not one of the club's bigger problems and turfing out a solid squad player when there are such glaring concerns across the pitch perhaps isn't a priority.

It remains to be seen whether Pochettino will revert to his Tottenham Hotspur days and occasionally employ wing-backs, or whether he will only use a back four at Old Trafford.

It has been revealed that amad is worth €45 million, as per Transfermarkt. United face Liverpool when Premier League action resumes this weekend.

Two Iranian men were found guilty of spying on dissident journalists in Britain on behalf of Iran's Revolutionary Guard on Thursday.

British counterterrorism police stated the case reflected intensifying hostile Iranian activity in the country, an issue that recently made headlines amid the security scare at the RAF Fairford airbase that's a major operational site in Europe for the US Air Force.

The men, both in their 40s, were arrested last year, with Iran repeatedly rejecting the allegations against them.

The Woolwich Crown Court in London convicted one of the Iranian citizens not just of spying on journalists working for the Persian-language dissident TV channel Iran International, but of plotting a violent attack against one or more of them.

The second individual had also faced charges of plotting an attack but was only convicted of spying on the reporters.

One of the convicted defendants mentioned he was acting under duress after his family was threatened, and the other said he did not know that his actions were assisting Iranian intelligence.

A third defendant, a 57-year-old Iranian man, was acquitted of all charges.

The men were accused of engaging in conduct likely to assist the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), Iran's multi-discipline military force that's seen as closer to the country's religious leadership and more influential than its regular armed forces.

The UK formally designated the IRGC as a threat to national security in July, meaning that supporting or assisting the organization can carry penalties of up to 14 years in prison as part of latest rules on national security and state threats.

Sentencing in this case is still pending and is scheduled for mid-December.

"This was a calculated operation to spy on those critical of the Iranian regime," said Frank Ferguson, chief prosecutor for the Crown Prosecution Service's special crime and counter-terrorism division.

The two men were accused of visiting addresses linked to their targets, taking photos and videos, and using platforms such as ChatGPT to research them online.

"Thankfully, the defendants were stopped before any attack could take place," prosecutor Ferguson remarked.

Senior ‌National Coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing Vicki Evans noted that the IRGC or "middlemen" for Iranian intelligence were directing the plot.

Iran's government had repeatedly denied the allegations, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying he was "disturbed" by the trio's arrests last May.

There have been four cases targeting the Persian language television channel Iran International since late 2023.

In July, two Romanian men were jailed for stabbing a journalist outside his home in 2024.

A spokesman for the broadcaster's parent firm, Volant Media, said in a statement that Thursday's verdicts "don't make the lives of our journalists any safer so long as the Islamic Republic of Iran continues its campaign of death threats and violence against them.".

Iran International reported that a British barrister was also one of the targets.

British law enforcement has been warning of an uptick of hostile Iranian activity in recent years, particularly since the US military operations against Tehran began earlier this year.

Most notably, the UK has accused Iran of being behind a suspected plot targeting the RAF Fairford base in September, after which US President Donald Trump withdrew some long-range bombers from the site.

Three men were indicted in the US in relation to that plot this week, while two others currently face charges in the UK.

Industry observers note that but beyond this, the head of Britain's MI5 domestic intelligence agency Ken MacCullum mentioned in October that Iran-linked operations had led to more than 50 arrests in the last year. He also said known cases of so-called state threats had more than quadrupled in a decade.

Counter-terrorism police chief Evans mentioned she expected this trend to continue.

France this week also accused Iran of being behind a cyberattack targeting refrigeration units at hundreds of supermarkets in October, although Iran denied any involvement.

European governments are on heightened alert for so-called hybrid warfare tactics, from Russia as well as Iran, amid the geopolitical tensions of recent years. New technologies like low-cost drones and AI are also threatening to make such activities cheaper, harder to trace, and potentially more effective.

Latest Update: Mauricio Pochettino will leave USMNT for Manchester United after Haiti matches

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mauricio Pochettino will officially join Manchester United after the current United States men's national team camp concludes, bringing an end to his two-year tenure in the job that was headlined by this year's World Cup on home soil.His final games in charge will be the two-legged Concacaf Nations League semifinals against Haiti, the first of which will take place on Saturday at Miami's Nu Stadium while the second will be on Tuesday at Cincinnati's TQL Stadium.
  • For the USMNT, the timing is awkward.
  • Recent findings suggest that "That news kind of got sprung on us, like the rest of the world, I'd say," Robinson said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino will officially join Manchester United after the current United States men's national team camp concludes, bringing an end to his two-year tenure in the job that was headlined by this year's World Cup on home soil.His final games in charge will be the two-legged Concacaf Nations League semifinals against Haiti, the first of which will take place on Saturday at Miami's Nu Stadium while the second will be on Tuesday at Cincinnati's TQL Stadium.

For the USMNT, the timing is awkward. Though the next World Cup is still four years away, Pochettino signed a fresh four-year deal in August and is right now with the team at U.S. Soccer's national training center in the suburbs of Atlanta. He spent the week with the USMNT while his representatives worked out a deal for him to join United.

Recent findings suggest that "That news kind of got sprung on us, like the rest of the world, I'd say," Robinson said. "Similar things happened in the past, happened at the World Cup where huge teams lose their manager and they start looking at possible candidates and for us to have a manager who's linked with those sorts of jobs means we're very lucky to work with a top-level manager but it never seems to leak into the work we do, whether it's the World Cup or whether it's going to be this camp.".

Industry observers note that pochettino was the first USMNT head coach with genuine international appeal, U.S. Soccer more often than not picking from a domestic talent pool in the team's modern history. His tenure has reflected just that – he became the federation's highest-paid coach ever when he initially joined in 2024, the salary and the scope of his role only increasing in his recent contract extension. U.S. Soccer surprisingly plucked him out of the European club game, where he had spent the entirety of his coaching career beforehand, making a name for himself at Tottenham Hotspur before later stops at Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea. Naturally, clubs of that ilk never lost interest and over the course of his time with the USMNT, he was linked to a handful of jobs. The most notable approach came from AC Milan, who were considering the move in the build-up to the World Cup but ultimately hired ex-Manchester United coach Ruben Amorim instead.

"Even when we first met a couple summers ago, there were lots of other people interested in having Mauricio and team join," U.S. Soccer CEO J.T. Batson stated in May. "He had standing offers from other places to come. He wanted to be here. He's a major believer in what we're doing at U.S. Soccer. He's a big believer in soccer in America and he's a big believer in this men's team and so, throughout this entire process, when you have top-class talent, whether it's salespeople, whether it's marketing people or whether it's coaches, other organizations want them and throughout this, Mauricio and team have been incredibly transparent. They've been great partners and are, of course, excited about the summer … There's been a longer list of outreach than what has even been reported and so they've been great about that.".

Pochettino has also been open about his desire to return to the Premier League during his stint with the USMNT, something the move to United will accomplish.

United are at the moment in the relegation zone with one win in 10 games, the least of any team in the Premier League this season.

Sources indicate that pochettino's track record with the USMNT is not exactly notable – he has 21 wins in 45 games, nearly all of them against teams below them in the FIFA rankings. They stumbled in a variety of ways when they attempted to punch above their weight, most notably in the World Cup round of 16 loss to Belgium that was tinged by the Folarin Balogun affair. His attempts to lead the USMNT to a statement-making run at a World Cup on home soil were mixed at best, since the team could not pass the last 16 hurdle they have been stuck at since 2010, but Pochettino still found a way to recalibrate the U.S. team in his two years in charge.

According to recent reports, the specifics of the round of 16 elimination were a surprise, even if the exit was not. The U.S. team's player pool, talented as it was at the World Cup, was not considered amongst the world's elites so a genuinely deep run over the summer felt improbable. Pochettino, though, managed to get the best out of the group and had the USMNT playing in a way it rarely had previously – in an entertaining, high-intensity, attack-minded system. The style is a hallmark of Pochettino's coaching career but has been historically difficult to integrate at the international level, with teams usually gathering for 10 days at a time, weeks or months apart, and has historically not been the USMNT's strategy. Pochettino's predecessor Gregg Berhalter, for example, was more reserved in his tactical approach and before him, the U.S. team were known more for grit than style.

Slowly but surely, Pochettino's approach worked with the generation of players Berhalter brought in. He correctly identified that the player pool's strengths were in attack, forwards Balogun and Christian Pulisic continuing to serve as central figures for the team. More notably, though, Pochettino found use for players Berhalter had previously cast aside – midfielder Malik Tillman became a key player, his versatility something Pochettino counted as an asset. Forward Ricardo Pepi also rose up the ranks in the build-up to the World Cup, his first after being one of the last omissions from Berhalter's 2022 team.

Industry observers note that pochettino's legacy might actually be the player pool shakeup he oversaw on the road to the World Cup, which felt rushed because of the short timeline but was ultimately useful. Defender Alex Freeman was the breakout of the Pochettino years, going from relative obscurity at Orlando City to a World Cup starter and goalscorer in less than 500 days. Midfielder Sebastian Berhalter, the son of Pochettino's predecessor, was not on the national team's radar until his first call-up in 2025 and looks like a national team fixture for years to come. The player pool expansion project will only get more exciting from here with the USMNT's up-and-comers, with some like Cavan Sullivan and Adri Mehmeti poised to be some of the best players in the history of the men's program.

The coach's departure will sting in some ways, but his tenure ensured that the USMNT would be in a position of strength, which was hardly the case when he arrived. He inherited a team that had lost its way after a group stage exit in the Copa America and will leave behind a team with a clear enough roadmap to the 2030 World Cup. The Pochettino years prove that the next head coach should primarily be a strong tactical fit, no matter the candidate's global appeal, because he was right to identify that an attack-minded approach would suit the player pool. That's especially true with the up-and-comers since many of the brightest prospects are attackers.

Recent findings suggest that there is no reason U.S. Soccer should not hire the best fit for the job but for perhaps the first time in the program's history, the USMNT's prospects might truly rest with the players at their disposal. Pochettino's successor will be chiefly tasked with getting the best out of them, much as he did with the U.S. team's core. As an exciting generation of talent finds their footing with the senior team, that's exactly how it should be.

#82875. Can Mauricio Pochettino replicate hallmark intensity he brought to USMNT with Manchester United?

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1146 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

Can Mauricio Pochettino replicate hallmark intensity he brought to USMNT with Manchester United?

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1146 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • From the jump, we should say, physical metrics are not going to tell you the whole story about any player, team or tactical system.
  • Sources indicate that too often, sprints are used as a proxy for effort when anyone who has even passing familiarity with the sport of soccer knows better.
  • Industry observers note that manchester United didn't slide into the bottom three because they were eating up less ground per game, 112.5 kilometers to be precise, than 18 of the other 19 teams in the Premier League this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From the jump, we should say, physical metrics are not going to tell you the whole story about any player, team or tactical system. Indeed, there is such potential for misdiagnosis when assessing running statistics that senior figures at more than one of the best recruiting clubs in England consider their worth to be, at best, dubious.

Sources indicate that too often, sprints are used as a proxy for effort when anyone who has even passing familiarity with the sport of soccer knows better. You know who didn't have to peg it all that often? Sergio Busquets, perhaps the best defensive midfielder of his generation, plying his trade for the majority of his career at Barcelona. Keep the ball, read the game, control the territory and you will very quickly find the other team covering plenty more kilometers than you.

Industry observers note that manchester United didn't slide into the bottom three because they were eating up less ground per game, 112.5 kilometers to be precise, than 18 of the other 19 teams in the Premier League this season. If there were any correlation between distance covered and results, then the relegation race would be even more exciting than it is shaping up to be, given that Liverpool sit below United on that measure and Manchester City above them. It is quite hard to believe that United are winning fewer games compared to last year (when they had nearly 10% less possession it should be noted) because each player is covering about 45 meters fewer per game. Physical data might not be linked to team quality, then, but it might tell us something relevant if, for instance, United were to hire a coach who prizes dynamic players and demands an intense press at the very top of the pitch. A Mauricio Pochettino type, if you will. The soon-to-be former United States men's national team head coach, handed the task of extricating Manchester United from the relegation zone before molding a contender, is defined by the aggression and energy of his charges. It is why he was the perfect match for a young Tottenham side with a point to prove. It is why Paris Saint-Germain and the Neymar-Kylian Mbappe axis was such an obviously awkward fit from the off.

Industry observers note that it is also a template that has worked even when there was cause for skepticism. You couldn't have players sprinting their way across SoFi after the rigors of a club season, noted those who doubted the USMNT. He didn't ask much of his team, just "to use your brain while physically, you were killing yourself," as Tim Ream, then 38, said in the summer.

Tell you what, though, it worked. The United States' World Cup campaign might have ended at about the time and in the fashion that most expected, but at their best, they were pressing dynamos. Their 10.16 passes allowed per defensive action (PPDA) -- a measure of press intensity -- placed them sixth among the 48 teams at the World Cup, rubbing shoulders with the likes of Germany, Spain and Uruguay, coached by Pochettino's mentor and high priest of the high press Marcelo Bielsa. No team that reached the knockouts forced their opponents to misplace a higher proportion of their passes than the U.S., 22.8%.

Pochettino might have framed much of his work around changing the culture of the USMNT, but that was a job that was easier to do with a player pool that suited his needs. His squad was strong, organized and, most importantly of all, athletic.

That is not a term that is particularly associated with Manchester United. Indeed, according to Gradient Sports, one of the leading external providers of physical data in football, Pochettino's upcoming team is the least athletic in the Premier League. Based on Gradient's athleticism score -- which combines a host of physical data points including accelerations and decelerations, sprint distance and max speed -- United and Nottingham Forest are cut adrift from the rest of the league. In average max speed of outfield players, United also rank 19th out of 20, 5% slower than the fleet-footed Bournemouth and Liverpool.

It has been revealed that the months to come may prove that United look unathletic because that's how Michael Carrick wanted them to play, controlling possession and building more steadily than the sides who rushed headfirst into any counter that came their way. Instinctively, though, that does not feel like the United of Harry Maguire, Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo, does it?

Recent findings suggest that the three center backs who have started the bulk of United's Premier League games this season -- Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Ayden Heaven -- all rank around the bottom third or lower of players in their position in terms of top speed, accelerations and decelerations and percentage of runs at high speeds (20-25 km/h), according to Gradient data. It is a similar story for the midfielders, particularly Andrey Santos, Mainoo and Tielemans. The one central midfield option with an impressive athletic profile, Carlos Baleba, is out injured. It seemed bitterly ironic that Baleba's hamstring went after a driving run through midfield. The sheer act of high-intensity running does sometimes look like it puts an unbearable strain on United legs.

In a recent development, that might be why they do it so little. Opta judges that Santos applies pressure to 56.2% of his opponents' touches, Tielemans 56.8%, Bruno Fernandes 57% and Mainoo 57.3%. All of them sit in the bottom 12 in the league among midfielders with 300 or more minutes. Marcus Rashford, Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Amad Diallo occupy spots one, three, five and six in terms of the top flight's least pressing-y forwards.

Now, of course, Pochettino can adapt. After all, he has just implemented a surprisingly effective high press in a side captained by Ream (sorry, Tim!). A lot of the Chelsea squad he took over in 2023-24 did not look to be at ease hunting the ball, but he still had them above league average in PPDA, opponent pass completion, ball recoveries and in particular duel success in the final third. A bit more oomph is not beyond these United players, as they indicated last season.

Industry observers note that however, it is particularly curious to finally alight on Pochettino, whom they could have hired at least half a dozen times in the past, when the squad seems so ill-suited to his principles. We might not be able to tell from physical data whether this team was giving its all for Carrick -- and, by extension, whether there is another gear for the new manager to drive them to -- but what we can see is certainly enough to raise the question of why the powers that be at United think that this is a squad ready to play Pochettino-style.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Everton midfielder Leon Osman has praised David Moyes’ enduring legacy in the blue half of Merseyside, insisting the Scotsman’s Glaswegian grit made him the ideal fit the club.

Moyes transformed Everton’s fortunes during an 11-year spell on Merseyside between 2002 and 2013, consistently guiding the Toffees into the top half of the Premier League despite operating on a fraction of the transfer budgets enjoyed by their top-flight rivals.

While Moyes never lifted a major trophy during his tenure - falling just short in the 2009 FA Cup final against Chelsea - Osman believes his former boss’s ability to punch above his weight cements his status as one of the club’s most vital modern figures.

"For the majority of David Moyes' time in charge of Everton, he's probably overachieved in terms of what he's had to spend in the transfer market, so while he might not have had the success Harry Catterick did in terms of silverware, he's been so key for the club," Osman told Betway.

"He's a great fit for Everton, and I think it's that Glaswegian way that adapts particularly well to Liverpool because there's a real understanding of what the people of the city are like and what they want to see from their football team. Everton is the people's club first and foremost, and the fans want to see the team work hard and show that desire to be successful and that's something David Moyes has always instilled in his teams.".

It has been revealed that osman was a central pillar of that Moyes era, making over 400 appearances for his boyhood club after breaking into the senior squad under the manager’s guidance. However, the former England international admitted he initially faced an uphill battle to prove he possessed the physicality required for top-flight football before becoming one of Moyes' most trusted lieutenants.

"He's the man who gave me my shot in the Premier League, so I'll always be thankful to him for that," Osman added. "It did take me a while, though, to convince him I was able and I was ready to play at that level, but once he gave me that chance I think he realised that we had very similar outlooks in terms of style of play and how the game should be played and we had a really great relationship throughout my career.".

AI is turbocharging cyberattacks — can computer scientists catch up?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Artificial intelligence systems are transforming the way software vulnerabilities are discovered.Credit: Hailshadow/Getty.
  • The disruption of multiple computer systems run by Microsoft, US air traffic control, the bank JPMorgan Chase and even the US National Security Agency has renewed concerns about the resilience of critical digital infrastructure.
  • At the same time, researchers have reported artificial intelligence -assisted discovery of security flaws in Java and PHP software, while hackers have used AI tools to target supermarket fridges and freezers in Europe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Artificial intelligence systems are transforming the way software vulnerabilities are discovered.Credit: Hailshadow/Getty.

The disruption of multiple computer systems run by Microsoft, US air traffic control, the bank JPMorgan Chase and even the US National Security Agency has renewed concerns about the resilience of critical digital infrastructure.

At the same time, researchers have reported artificial intelligence -assisted discovery of security flaws in Java and PHP software, while hackers have used AI tools to target supermarket fridges and freezers in Europe.

Industry observers note that although probably unrelated, these incidents highlight a broader transformation in cybersecurity, say researchers. Artificial intelligence is changing how software vulnerabilities are discovered, allowing both attackers and security specialists to examine vast quantities of computer code at unprecedented speed.

Industry observers note that “I think vulnerability discovery without AI is basically dead,” says Steven Murdoch, a computer security researcher at University College London. Researchers in the field who don’t use the technology now risk falling behind, he says.

Recent findings suggest that AI can find weaknesses in software much faster than humans can, giving attackers time to exploit vulnerabilities before organizations can fix them. Researchers now want to understand how thoroughly AI can check software for security flaws, and whether it could introduce latest weaknesses.

According to recent reports, agentic systems help attackers identify security vulnerabilities more rapidly and systematically. While hackers previously had to spend hours inspecting websites and probing software for weaknesses that offered unauthorized access to networks, AI agents use automated tools that can search millions of lines of computer code.

Google has reported that attackers have already used agentic AI to examine software updates, identify the security problems they address, and then find ways to exploit them.

NEWS: Cyberattacks are hitting research institutions — with devastating effects.

NEWS: Cyberattacks are hitting research institutions — with devastating effects.

Recent findings suggest that “For me, it's about the scale,” says Daniel Gardham, a cybersecurity researcher at the University of Surrey. AI tends to find the same kinds of weaknesses as human hackers, but it makes it easier for people with limited technical expertise to break into systems.

“They can set an AI agent off and come back in 20 minutes and have dozens of results already,” he notes.

In a recent development, even with AI, most security breaches still involve human failure, he states, such as weak passwords (a common problem with Europe’s supermarket freezers was that passwords were defaults such as ‘admin’ or ‘12345’) or clicking on links from unfamiliar sources. AI-crafted messages can make such phishing messages more convincing and so more likely to succeed. They can draw on publicly available information to personalize fraudulent communications and make them appear authentic.

Murdoch says AI is particularly good at discovering familiar kinds of software flaws, even if the most accomplished human researchers remain better at finding entirely new types of weakness. “They don't need to sleep,” he says. “You can happily work a hundred of them in parallel.”.

Recent findings suggest that these capabilities of AI helped discover security flaws in Java and PHP software, two programming languages that build cross-platform software and websites. In the Java case, for example, AI identified circumstances that could allow an attacker to corrupt computer memory. But Murdoch says the significance of the concern has been exaggerated.

The Java vulnerability, he says: “Is a real problem, but it’s not one of the top ten vulnerabilities this year or probably even this week.”.

Industry observers note that just like hackers, cybersecurity researchers are using AI tools to rapidly and efficiently find weaknesses in computer systems. Murdoch states this has become increasingly crucial to vulnerability researchers, who can now examine much larger quantities of software and work out how to patch up the defences where necessary. Researchers are also developing AI agents that can detect and repair vulnerabilities automatically.

When security researchers uncover a weakness, they typically notify the software developer privately, allowing engineers to prepare a remedy before publishing details of the problem.

AI is set to completely transform cybersecurity — here’s how researchers must prepare.

AI is set to completely transform cybersecurity — here’s how researchers must prepare.

Murdoch says the use of AI in cyber security has shortened the time window between public disclosure and attempted exploitation – from several weeks, to just a few days.

Recent findings suggest that rushing an upgrade can bring its own problems. A software patch can interfere with other programs and cause the sort of outage that organisations are trying to avoid.

“The life for the defenders who are trying to fix things has become significantly harder,” Murdoch claims.

Industry observers note that it’s unlikely that the recent tech outages were connected as large-scale cyber-attack, says Murdoch. The most prominent disruptions, he says, are likely technical malfunctions rather than anything more sinister.

It's the international break, and it's usually a quiet week in the world of soccer. Well, it wasn't the case. USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino will leave the American national team after the two Nations League's matches against Haiti and will become the upcoming manager of Manchester United, after the Red Devils declared the sacking of Michael Carrick. Pochettino, who was hired by the USMNT in 2024, will make his comeback in the Premier League after coaching Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. I'm Francesco Porzio with the latest.

Saturday, Nov. 14🇺🇸 NWSL semifinal: Washington Spirit vs. Utah Royals, 12 p.m. ➡️ CBS, Paramount+🇺🇸 CONCACAF Nations League: Haiti vs. United States, 4:30 p.m. ➡️ TNT, HBO Max🇺🇸 USL League One Final: Charlotte Independence vs. Athletic Club Boise, 7:30 p.m. ➡️ CBS Sports Golazo Network.

It has been revealed that now the big question is about who will be the successor of Pochettino at the national team. With a new national training center, an established team, and young players coming up from everywhere to push that squad, it's a job that should be an attractive one to managers around the world, depending on the direction that U.S. Soccer wants to go. Pochettino was an appropriate splashy hire ahead of the World Cup, and it's not surprising that a top team in the world still wanted him. But when looking to build a stable base for 2030, there's a chance that the powers that be would prefer a candidate who would be more bought into American soccer. Here's some of the names that our own Chuck Booth wrote down:.

Sources indicate that steve Cherundolo, U.S. U-23s: At the moment overseeing the U-23s, the former Los Angeles FC manager would likely be in the USMNT succession plan for Pochettino. The goal was to bring both camps together as much as possible and ensure that they had a similar style, as plenty of players would go between both squads depending on needs. The issue is that this has all happened faster than anyone would've anticipated, since if Steve Cherundolo was going to take over the USMNT, that'd likely be a 2028 post-Olympic deal rather than right at this moment. But also looking at the performance of LAFC without Cherundolo, it's clear that he held things together plenty in that squad and that he could be a fit for the role; the question is just when.

It has been revealed that pep Guardiola, free agent: You have to make the call, and it looks like they will. We all know what the answer likely is, but if there's an opening and the USMNT wants the best manager available, Pep Guardiola is right there. The former Manchester City, Bayern Munich and Barcelona boss is expected to be their top target, according to The Athletic. They reportedly called Jurgen Klopp before hiring Pochettino, and this would be a similar scenario as Klopp is now with Germany. Guardiola isn't going to stay out of management forever, so why not try to bring him back in on the road to 2030? He would be facing similar issues to Pochettino of not knowing if he'll be a long-term fit for the role, but those aren't things that should come into play if the goal is to hire the best available manager who is a fit for the job.

Recent findings suggest that roberto Martinez, free agent: A name that came up after the World Cup when decisions were being made on whether Pochettino should be extended, Roberto Martinez could come into consideration yet again. On paper, he offers a mix of European experience and the staying power of someone who has overseen multiple international sides for an entire cycle, but it's tough to say he'd be a good fit. Martinez wasn't able to lead Belgium's golden generation to a title and struggled to get Portugal to play to their talent as well. With a USMNT that have the world at their feet as young players begin to lead the way, it'd be better to go the domestic route before turning to Martinez.

Andoni Iraola looked up to the ceiling of Fenerbahce’s media auditorium as he tried to find the words to describe the madness he had just witnessed.

Sources indicate that “Cheap” was his first conclusion, swiftly followed by “messy”; technically, Liverpool’s head coach was right but this was a moment when nobody would have found glitch had he gone further. “Absurd” and “preposterous” would have been more accurate portrayals of this calamity.

Roy Hodgson, in August 2010, was the last Anfield manager to oversee a win here and there was an irony that the hero of that night in Trabzon – Dirk Kuyt – masterminded this downfall.

In a recent development, andoni Iraola states he will not waste any more time thinking about the penalty Liverpool were denied against Arsenal and won’t seek an explanation from Pro Ref. There was a significant fallout following the 1-0 loss at Anfield on Sunday with many judges believing Stuart Attwell, who was VAR, should have consulted match official Andy Madley to highlight an obvious pull by Jurrien Timber that prevented Alexander Isak heading a Bradley Barcola cross.

Liverpool’s head coach explained in the heat of the moment that he would tell his players to go down if they felt contact in the area and Cody Gakpo, the Netherlands international, explained last night in Istanbul it was a message the squad had taken on board.

“As a team, we play pretty fair – maybe we should dive some more like the gaffer remarked,” Gakpo, who also had claims to be awarded a penalty against Arsenal, explained. “On both occasions you could have given a penalty or a foul, but they decided not. We have to live with the decision. That’s it.”.

But as angry as he was with the situation, Iraola has drawn a line on the matter. He is not going to seek out Pro Ref for a discussion – even though he feels a number of decisions have gone against Liverpool this season – and is channelling his energy into other situations.

Iraola noted: “I didn’t ask for an explanation and I haven’t received an explanation, no. I told you what you I think about the plays but, honestly, I don’t have the time to [speak to Pro Ref]. I have been preparing for Fenerbahce. It is just two days between games so I have just been focusing on this game and the opposition and how to prepare the team.”.

Liverpool have made the long trip to Turkey to take on Fenerbahce on matchday four of the Champions League.

Liverpool enter this fixture having won all three Champions League matches thus far, beating Atletico Madrid, LASK and Villarreal to make it nine points from nine for Andoni Iraola’s side. Liverpool’s five-game unbeaten streak was ended by Arsenal in the league on Sunday. They return to the city where the club enjoyed one of their most memorable nights, beating AC Milan in the Champions League final 21 years ago.

Sources indicate that “Istanbul is always going to be very special for Liverpool,” Iraola noted. “It is difficult to find a more important night. Tomorrow [tonight] it won’t be easy, you talk about statistics, especially English teams playing here. They have very good players and a very good squad, they know how to play in this competition. We have to start strong in the game. It is very early in the season to establish comparisons. We want to continue how we have done in the Champions League, three games and nine points, it is a good chance to get to 12 points and then finish in the top eight. Champions League away is very difficult.”.

In addition to the long-term absentees Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Giovanni, both Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong have missed the trip to Turkey.

Fenerbahce have made a slow start to their Champions League campaign, taking just two points from their opening three fixtures. They have drawn twice against Roma and Slavia Prague at home whilst they suffered a heavy 6-0 loss at Aston Villa. Former Liverpool forward Dirk Kuyt has been appointed their interim coach following the resignation of Ismail Kartal following their recent defeat to arch rivals Galatasaray just over a week ago.

According to recent reports, “It is a great opportunity for us to show what we can do,” Kuyt stated. “It is also a great opportunity for me, a game between two teams that are very important to me. We have a very good plan, and we have to believe in this plan. No-one who loves Fenerbahce is happy with the current situation, but this is a huge opportunity. We have players who have won the Champions League and the World Cup.”.

Recent findings suggest that they come into tonight’s match having lost back-to-back league games since drawing against Slavia Prague on matchday three of the Champions League. They have plenty of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Ederson, N’Golo Kante and Romelu Lukaku.

Hungary eases abortion restrictions in women's rights overhaul

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (427 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hungary on Thursday stated it would ease abortion rules and ratify an international treaty on violence against women.
  • Under the planned changes to the so-called "heartbeat regulation," women will no longer be forced to listen to the vital signs of the fetus before an abortion.
  • Women will also be able to get emergency contraceptive pills without prescription.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hungary on Thursday stated it would ease abortion rules and ratify an international treaty on violence against women.

Under the planned changes to the so-called "heartbeat regulation," women will no longer be forced to listen to the vital signs of the fetus before an abortion.

Women will also be able to get emergency contraceptive pills without prescription.

The changes proposed by the new government under Prime Minister Peter Magyar are a significant break with the conservative policies of his predecessor Viktor Orban.

The country also plans to ratify the Istanbul Convention, a treaty aimed at preventing violence against women and domestic violence.

It has been revealed that hungarian law allows for most abortions to be performed up to 12 weeks, and up to 24 weeks in cases of severe developmental abnormalities. Until now, women were required to have a medical provider show them evidence of a definitive sign of fetal life, commonly understood as the so-called "fetal heartbeat," before deciding whether to have an abortion.

The controversial 2022 policy had received widespread criticism from doctors and women’s rights groups as being cruel and humiliating. It will now be scrapped.

The policy had not led to a decline in abortions and according to Magyar, had raised "serious bioethical questions.".

The second major change is that emergency contraception will be available without prescription.

Further measures include changing the criminal code aimed at better protecting women, including making the misuse of intimate images a criminal offense and strengthening the treatment of victims of domestic violence during criminal proceedings.

Sources indicate that hungary also looks to ratify an international treaty on the protection of women which most other EU members have long ratified. The Istanbul Convention came into force in 2014 and, among other things, requires rape to be criminalized based on the absence of freely given consent.

"We are making it clear that sexual acts can only ⁠take ​place with the voluntary consent of the other party," ​Magyar said.

The government of his predecessor Orban had opposed the treaty, arguing that it promoted what it described as "gender ideology.".

"We are making a clear and accountable commitment to putting an end to the era of inaction," Magyar said in a Facebook video.

Among the EU’s other members, only Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Lithuania and Slovakia have not yet ratified the convention.

The Istanbul Convention is a treaty by the Council of Europe, an international organization that promotes human rights and the rule of law across Europe and includes more countries than the member of the EU.

#82858. Mauricio Pochettino's USMNT farewell was inevitable but it hurts all the same: 'A major thank you from my heart'
