📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After two runner-up finishes at the NWSL Championship, the Washington Spirit will get a third consecutive shot at lifting the big prize.

The Washington Spirit rallied from an early deficit to defeat the Utah Royals 2-1 in front of another sold-out Audi Field. The Spirit weathered the fastest goal in NWSL playoff history, then flipped the script within minutes and never took their foot off the pedal or lost control. Utah Royals' Cloe Lacasse struck first on the scoreboard, and Sofia Cantore and Clara Luvanga provided the decisive goals for the Spirit, while Trinity Rodman brought plenty of spark and Andi Sullivan supplied reliable, steady play in the midfield.

Here's how the Spirit rallied for the win:.

Industry observers note that the Royals arrived in D.C. early in the week, avoiding a nationwide flight stoppage on Friday, and fresh off a huge quarterfinal upset -- a 1-0 win against the No. 2 seed San Diego Wave FC. They wasted little time to show their early playoff win was no fluke.

Sources indicate that in the opening two minutes, Utah won a corner kick, and Lacasse created multiple moments of history. Her service into the box curled toward the near post, creating some miscommunication between goalkeeper Sandy MacIver and her defenders, and the ball snuck into the net. It was the fastest goal scored in NWSL playoff history and the first-ever olimpico scored in the postseason.

CLOÉ LACASSE OLIMPICO IN THE SECOND MINUTE 😱@UtahRoyalsFC off to a FLYING start the @NWSL semifinal!Watch the action LIVE on @CBS and @paramountplus! pic.twitter.com/UfWxDcSB5Y.

Recent findings suggest that the early breakthrough stunned the typically rowdy crowd, though the set-piece tally was hardly a surprise, considering Utah's ability this year. The squad scored 15 goals off set pieces this season, with seven headed goals, so Lacasse's ability to score from the flag was just one more highlight for its set-piece playbook.

The early lead should have been a boost for the visiting side, but instead, it opened up the game; the Spirit then tested the Royals with relentless attacking pressure.

It has been revealed that the Spirit needed just six minutes to turn things around. Washington's attacking trio combined for the equalizer, with Luvanga finding Rodman out wide in space, and the winger swiftly connecting with Cantore in front of goal.

SOFIA CANTORE WITH THE BACKHEEL 🤯Her seventh goal of 2026 is her first playoff goal to bring @WashSpirit level 1-1!Watch the action LIVE on @CBS and @paramountplus! pic.twitter.com/C8J63tVzQn.

"I think getting scored on in the first few minutes will really humble you, and a little bit of a wake-up call, but I thought our response was incredible right after and all game long," Sullivan said after the game.

"As soon as we responded after the goal, I think even when we got scored on, I had full confidence that we would get it done," she said.

Sullivan's role in controlling the game as the Spirit closed out the first half was notable. She's the longest-tenured player on the active Spirit roster right now, with goalkeeper Aubrey Kingsbury out on maternity leave. Sullivan herself returned to the squad after an ACL injury and then maternity leave. The defensive midfielder completed all of her tackles (three) and aerial challenges (four) and captained the team on the pitch.

"She represents a lot of the values that we want to have as a team, as a club, on and off the field, and right now she's reaching that peak of performance. I'm very, very happy and proud of her because it's been tough for her. Obviously, coming from a long injury, and then maternity leave. So being able to come back to get fit again and try to compete at this level; it's not easy, and she's a role model. An example as a captain with the young players, fresh players, and being able to do a lot of things," Spirit head coach Adrian Gonzalez said after the game.

"Whatever the team needs, she's kind of that voice. Very happy and proud of her because I know what this means to her and also for us. Having her again and being able to play a final is huge for her and for us," he stated.

Sources indicate that while Utah managed to stave off attacking sequences by the Spirit to close out the opening half, the Spirit's game-winning goal came in the early minutes of the second half. A poor back pass by Utah in their own half was the final dagger. Luvanga pounced on the mistimed pass, and a smart touch inside the box beat goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn.

Recent findings suggest that CLARA LUVANGA POUNCED ON THIS PASS 😮‍💨Her second goal in her second playoff match and the @WashSpirit are one step closer to returning to the @NWSL Final!Watch the semifinal LIVE on @CBS and @paramountplus! pic.twitter.com/f0uUfUU19K.

The Tanzanian international has only been on the roster since September, but her impact on games has grown week to week, and now she can add a game-winning NWSL playoff goal to her resume.

Recent findings suggest that "It's not the first one that she scores like that. Obviously, she puts a lot of pressure on centerbacks, keepers, and that is very contagious. When you see that your forward is pushing and jumping and pressing like that. Everyone who is behind they follow her, and also creates a lot of doubts and nerves on the opponent team, not facilitating the build-up. And obviously, that was, I think, a big shot of energy," Gonzalez said after the game.

According to recent reports, "I think it was also a little bit of release, knowing that 'okay, we did the most difficult thing' that was coming back after we conceded a goal, and yeah, happy again because she's bringing a lot. Both attacking and defending, and obviously she's learning so quick and having a huge impact.".

According to recent reports, what's next The Spirit will face the winner of Sunday's semifinal between Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current. This will be the Spirit's third consecutive appearance in the NWSL Championship. When the league confirmed a neutral site for the 2026 NWSL Championship, it selected Audi Field, and now the Spirit have a chance to play in a home playoff final on Nov. 21.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Matthew Briggs became an instant pub quiz question in his very fist game in senior football.

By coming off the bench against Middlesbrough in May 2007, the Fulham left-back set a new Premier League record as its youngest-ever player.

Briggs inherited the distinction from Izzy Brown and would give it up to Harvey Elliott 12 years later, before Ethan Nwaneri set the mark at 15 years, 181 days in 2022.

But as Briggs told FourFourTwo: "Being the Premier League’s youngest player was one of the greatest moments and achievements of my life, but it came with a lot of pressure.

"When I eventually lost the title to Harvey Elliott after 12 long years - the longest anyone has had it - it felt like the pressure had been lifted and I could just be me.

"People had always been wondering why I wasn’t doing this and that, why I wasn’t achieving what they believed I should have been achieving.

"It’s a lot of noise to deal with. I have sympathy for Harvey Elliott now, too.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

I actually thought he was doing well at Liverpool, and he’s still young enough to get back to doing what he does best.".

Briggs believes that starting at such a high level so young can make the adaptation that much harder if you end up having to work your way back up the pyramid.

That's particularly true if your first move away comes as abruptly as it did for Briggs when he left Fulham for Millwall in 2014in the first permanent switch of his itinerant career.

Briggs explained: "I suffered a lot of injuries, although I was offered a three-year contract extension before I left Fulham.

"But Martin Jol got sacked, a upcoming manager came in and got rid of the whole team – I was injured at the time, and he wanted to bring in fresh blood. I’d been there since the age of 10.

"When you drop down the leagues, you have the aspiration to get back to the top, but when you get to a certain age, it’s harder to do that, especially when you’re suffering with injuries.

Recent findings suggest that "I suffered a lot with mental health because of that. Everything that was my superpower – speed, power, getting up and down the pitch, my body was stopping me from doing it.

Recent findings suggest that "I went to Denmark and really enjoyed my first season, but then my hip started playing up again and they told me I should retire, because I had no cartilage in my hip. I came back to the UK and played non-league for two more years, but my body just gave up.".

#82813. Super subs, xG kings and $150 million question marks: The Premier League's most intriguing players

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2292 w)
📖 Baca

Super subs, xG kings and $150 million question marks: The Premier League's most intriguing players

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2292 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Whatever you might think about the November international break, there is one fact you simply will not be bothered to argue against: it is well timed for the statistically-minded football fan in your life.
  • Sources indicate that we are not yet, then, at the stage where we can always draw hard and fast conclusions.
  • Industry observers note that spend $100 million on a player who turns 29 next week and the expectation is surely that a player will hit the ground running.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whatever you might think about the November international break, there is one fact you simply will not be bothered to argue against: it is well timed for the statistically-minded football fan in your life. A 10-game sample size -- that's the useful stuff. At this point, many but not all teams are what their analytics tell us they are. It's similar but not quite the same for players. Not many have hit the 900-minute mark yet, but plenty are at 500-plus, a body of evidence that usually isn't warped by any one good or bad game. Of course, it depends on how good or bad that game is.

Sources indicate that we are not yet, then, at the stage where we can always draw hard and fast conclusions. We are, however, in a position to find some interesting questions. Here are five of them, in player form:.

Industry observers note that spend $100 million on a player who turns 29 next week and the expectation is surely that a player will hit the ground running. That's especially true when they're Bruno Guimaraes, terror of Premier League midfields in a Newcastle United shirt, a player who had long since seemed ready to step up to a Champions League contender. While it would be fair to say that the Brazilian's form is nothing like a problem for table-topping Arsenal, he has not exactly started like a house on fire. Mikel Arteta has acknowledged as much whenever he has spoken about Guimaraes, even when served up the opportunity to praise him after what seemed an impressive performance against Hull City.

Sources indicate that "He's hitting serious levels now, but we can still take him to another level. That's my conviction; I told him that in the dressing room -- he owned a lot of moments in the game, but there is still much more to come." It would be fair to say that, Hull aside, the best levels he has hit have been as a substitute. When he comes off the bench, he passes more accurately, wins more tackles, creates chances and scores brilliant goals. As a starter, he has occasionally looked a beat off his teammates.

Recent findings suggest that physical data from Gradient Sports hints as to what the problem might be. For every 90 Premier League minutes on the field, Guimaraes covers less of it at sprint speed (≥25 km/h) than any outfield player bar Mikel Merino and spends notably more time jogging than anyone, an average of 30 minutes. Compare Guimaraes to Declan Rice, an admittedly vertiginous bar, and it is easy to see why the new guy looks off the pace.

Industry observers note that equally, it explains why he's such a compelling substitute. When the other 21 players on the pitch are flagging, Guimaraes' comparative physical issues go unexposed and he can run the show.

That's all well and good for now, but he can't carry on like this, can he? You would have to assume that Myles Lewis-Skelly will have to make way even if the academy graduate's emergence as a midfield option unlocked an improved Declan Rice at the tail end of last season. The second most expensive signing in your history can't be an impact guy off the bench behind the homegrown kid, right? Probably not, but if there's any team that could justify the idea of Guimaraes as a 12th man, maybe it's Arsenal, where they pride themselves on their game-changing finishers.

Erling Haaland's Swiftian reign at the top of the Premier League xG chart has been interrupted, at least temporarily, by an unlikely source. You'd have to go back to the days of a marauding Romelu Lukaku for the last time an Everton striker looked like they might rule the roost. Only once since the Belgian's departure has an Evertonian cleared 20 goals in all competitions. In the last five, even a dozen has been beyond this club.

Thierno Barry isn't there yet, but boy is he on the right trajectory. His 7.28 non-penalty expected goals (npxG) puts him 0.22 ahead of Haaland and nearly 2.5 npxG up on anyone else in the league. Expand the pool to Europe's top five leagues and he is breathing rarefied air behind the top four of Lamine Yamal, Donyell Malen, Raphinha and Kylian Mbappe, all of whom have the advantage that they are not playing for an upper midtable outfit in the continent's most competitive division. And in that environment, Barry is making the hardest thing in the sport look easy: getting good shots in prime locations.

If Barry were turning them in as often as he was getting them, Everton might be even higher than sixth. Still, six goals through 10 games is not to be sniffed at, particularly when the pressure on the 24-year-old was so intense. The bungling of a deadline-day move for Folarin Balogun, as Beto moved to Fiorentina, meant it was Barry or bust for David Moyes this season.

Perhaps it was an enforced show of faith for a player who was in and out of the XI last season, his first in England, that brought the best out of the former Villarreal man. His manager views the success in more straightforward terms. "He has settled down a bit more," noted Moyes after Barry's brace helped down Coventry. "His language, his understanding, his communication is much better and he has worked hard to get himself in those positions to score.".

It has been revealed that it is easy to see why getting the soft factors right might have been all that was required. Barry is the ideal striker for the modern Premier League. Tall, strong and mobile -- he ranks third among center forwards for top speed this season, per Gradient Sports -- he can serve as an outball when a press needs beating and then get in the box. He might not have the technical elegance of an Mbappe, but he makes his presence felt and occupies high-value spaces. That is more valuable than it sounds, as proven when James Tarkowski's howitzer from range deflected in off him. You might not like it, but this is what elite center forward play looks like. Long may it continue, at least as far as Everton are concerned.

According to recent reports, there are three types of underrated footballers. First, your common-or-garden-variety underrated footballers, often to be found plying their trade at Wolverhampton Wanderers or Burnley. Ashley Westwood, in that season, put up stupidly high xA numbers. Then there are the so-often-dubbed-underrated that they actually become a bit overrated. Leighton Baines. Lee Carsley. They don't have to play for Everton, but it does help. Olivier Giroud is another. See, not all Everton.

In a recent development, the most rarely spotted of the underrated is the chameleonic one, correctly pegged for a while, only to develop to the point that he is underrated in a completely different way to how he once was. Take Alex Iwobi. Some time ago, a consensus coalesced around the Nigeria international that he was a good player for a team at Fulham's level (and indeed Everton's). Any minute he was on the field, he would probably be delivering good performances for good Premier League teams.

According to recent reports, not anymore. Ten games in and Iwobi looks like one of the outstanding creative forces in the Premier League, critical to the march towards adequacy that Fulham have undertaken after a slow start to life with Alvaro Arbeloa.

Among true playmakers, Iwobi is one of the best at getting the ball into dangerous areas and creating for his teammates. Iwobi leads the league in expected assists with 2.95 and is tied with Bruno Fernandes for most passes completed into the penalty area. Only Pascal Gross has created more chances.

Sources indicate that those players can't match Iwobi when it comes to ball progression either. In terms of advancing the ball not just into the box but from deeper, Fulham's ball-playing fulcrum on the inside left channel has completed more progressive passes than anyone not named Declan Rice or Jan Paul van Hecke.

Industry observers note that when Iwobi broke through at Arsenal, he displayed a preternatural sense for how to keep attacks alive, the pass before the pass before the pass. Now a 30-year-old, Iwobi still does that more than he unpicks defenses. One cannot argue, however, that he is not putting his teammates in the right spot. It is just that not everyone quite appreciates how often he does so just yet, including his own supporters, who jeered Iwobi when he was substituted in the early-season defeat to Crystal Palace. Since then, he has responded to his critics in style, teeing up two or more shots in each of Fulham's last seven Premier League matches. If a few more of them had been converted, in fact, if any of them had been converted, then Iwobi might not still be underrated.

The upper reaches of the list of most expensive transfers of all time are hardly all bangers all the time, but of the biggest money moves in the sport's history there are only a handful where at such an early stage you find yourself wondering if anyone really understood what the blueprint was. Manchester City committed the best part of $150 million on Enzo Fernandez this summer, a fee only eclipsed by Neymar and Kylian Mbappe. Beyond a vague sense that it would be nice to give latest manager Enzo Maresca one of his favorite players, what was it they had in mind?

Sources indicate that we pointed out earlier in the season that the aggressive positioning of Fernandez in the 5-3 win over Sunderland looked extreme; at the time it seemed reasonable to view it as a reflection of a stretched-out, chaotic game. Maresca had, of course, unlocked more number 10-ish qualities in the Argentine at Chelsea, but surely that had been reflective of what that team needed, particularly as Cole Palmer went off the boil? Perhaps not. Fernandez keeps popping up in the sort of positions that leave Elliot Anderson on an island. It is one thing to view Anderson as the newly introduced Rodri, quite another to immediately throw the England international in at the deep end, tying a whole midfield together by force of will.

Of course you could sketch out a logic for why you might push Fernandez high. It is not so long ago that City deployed two playmakers in front of a sitting midfielder and they ruled the Premier League. Fernandez and Rayan Cherki aren't Kevin De Bruyne and David Silva though.

According to recent reports, maybe Cherki could be offering a level of creation on a par with City greats; he started well enough last season. In year two, he is creating lower-quality chances, his expected assists per 90 dropping by 50%, notably more than the slight uptick in the quality and quantity of shots he is taking. It's no surprise that Cherki is creating less when fewer of his touches are coming in the attacking third. The output has been there so far, five goals and two assists in nine Premier League games, but for that to continue, Maresca might want to be getting his No. 10 into more dangerous spots.

Sources indicate that instead, those seem to be going to Fernandez, who has not proven himself able to get the final-third production to justify his platforming. For every 100 touches he takes, he is delivering significantly less npxG+xA than in either of the previous two seasons. Meanwhile, he is less effective without the ball than he has been at any stage since coming to England. That's no wonder. If an opponent passes through City's frontline, then Fernandez does not have the mobility to get back.

As such, to enable themselves to get perhaps a shot or two more than they would get with Ayyoub Bouaddi or Mateo Kovacic next to Anderson, City have made themselves an even more vulnerable side to the counterattack, already giving up more fast-break openings than they did in 2020-21 or 2021-22. Carry on like this, and Fernandez will become one of those nine-figure transfers, the ones that live in infamy.

Sources indicate that it was a signing that delighted a city when it was unveiled in early August, and rightly so. Loaning Carl Rushworth from Brighton had been an inspired bit of business by Coventry City, the then-24-year-old goalkeeper anchoring the best defense in the division as Frank Lampard's side returned to the top flight for the first time in over a quarter of a century. A club-record £22 million fee seemed a snip for such a young talent.

According to recent reports, all of that is worth bearing in mind given the struggles Rushworth has endured this season: saving just 53.7% of shots he has faced, conceding 5.19 more goals than the xG value of the shots he has faced. The swagger of last season has been replaced by a sloppiness apparent in both the goals he conceded in the second half against Tottenham, weak gloves doing nothing to repel efforts that came at him a bit quicker and a bit sooner than they might have last year.

None of this needs to be a problem for Rushworth. In 2023-24, James Trafford was another highly touted young goalkeeper afforded a shot at the big time by Burnley. He was obliterated up and down the Premier League, his first touch in the division picking the ball out of the net off Erling Haaland. Those struggles were the making of him, as they have broken others. It'll be some time yet before we discover which way these past few months send Rushworth.

#82810. Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (814 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (814 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA), a tech giant would have to remind you before the free trial ends and get your explicit agreement before it can start charging you.
  • Industry observers note that the Commission presented the proposal on Wednesday.
  • "We haven't seen that kind of reform in consumer protection in the last 20 years," Agustin Reyna, director general of the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), told DW.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA), a tech giant would have to remind you before the free trial ends and get your explicit agreement before it can start charging you. The proposed law would also make it easier to cancel a subscription online and require reminders before certain contracts renew automatically.

Industry observers note that the Commission presented the proposal on Wednesday. It wants to give consumers more control over how much time and money they spend online.

"We haven't seen that kind of reform in consumer protection in the last 20 years," Agustin Reyna, director general of the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), told DW.

His organization pushed for stronger EU rules against manipulative online practices. He sees the proposal as a good starting point for tackling problems that frustrate consumers every day.

The proposal also includes a ban on manipulative marketing tactics, so-called "dark patterns." A concrete example: You are trying to reserve a hotel room and the website claims that only three are left, a potentially false claim to pressure you into buying.

It has been revealed that A concert ticket that gets more expensive while you're waiting in an online queue raises a different problem. The price could still go up in the process, but the seller would have to show the current price while you wait and tell you the maximum you could be asked to pay.

Online games that encourage users to spend their money to advance are also targeted. Children would no longer be able to pay to win or get to the next level of their online game.

Marketing and personalized ads would need to be clearly marked and restricted in the case of children. Consumers should get the option to switch off doomscrolling functions such as the autoplay of videos, showing one clip after the other. With these fresh rules, the EU wants to make apps and websites less addictive.

In a recent development, for Christoph Busch, an academic with a focus on consumer law and digital services based at Osnabrück University in Germany, the option to opt out doesn't go far enough. He argues that a version in which consumers actively have to choose to opt into those functions would be more effective.

Industry observers note that "But then there is always the question of proportionality," Busch noted. "And I think here the European legislators are trying to balance different interests.".

These competing interests are particularly visible in the gaming industry, where interest groups have warned that the proposed EU restrictions could hurt developers and leave players with fewer options to choose from.

Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation called the proposal "unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate," arguing that a ban on selling children features that help them win or advance is worded so broadly that it "could cover almost any purchase in a game.".

It has been revealed that for Busch, this argument doesn't hold. "If your business model is based on addictive design features, then maybe your business model has to be reviewed," he said.

Catalina Goanta, an associate professor of private law and technology at Utrecht University, emphasized in an interview with DW that "regulation can very easily slide into overregulation.".

Even though she believes that the DFA is a solid and reasonable compromise, she argues that prohibiting dark patterns and doomscrolling altogether would be too prohibitive. Many of the issues consumers right now face could be resolved by enforcing existing regulation more effectively, she mentioned.

She points to the fact that the EU has made a name for itself in the past by adding fresh rules and regulations that have made it more difficult to access the European market, especially for small online businesses.

BEUC director Agustin Reyna disagrees.

"Instead of having 27 different regulations to adhere to, companies will now only get one," Reyna stated.

For him, this speaks for simplification, especially when the responsibility for compliance is shared between online influencers and the platforms they publish on.

According to the newly introduced legislation, the EU would have the possibility to impose fines of up to six percent of a organization's global annual revenue should the company violate the law.

The European Parliament and the Council, which represents member state governments, still have to agree on the text and formally adopt it. All experts agree that in that process, changes are still very likely.

"It will be a difficult trialogue, especially in this climate of simplification and deregulation with a focus on strengthening European competitiveness," mentioned Christoph Busch. In that climate, it is not easy to add consumer rights, he adds.

Recent findings suggest that agustin Reyna is more optimistic. "The parliament is a divided house, much more than in the past," he says. "But consumer protection is a subject that brings parties together because it brings tangible outcomes to people.".

The Original Article was published on 01 July 2026.

Correction to: Nature https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10695-1 Published online 1 July 2026.

In the version of this article initially published, the reagent information for the DNA2 inhibitor was incorrectly reported as DNA2i; Sigma-Aldrich, SML4192 and should instead have read DNA2i; NSC-105808. The change affects the Methods “Thymidine analogue incorporation” section and the Supplementary Table 7 reagents sheet. The error has been corrected in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

  • Whoever put that £35million release clause in Youri Tielemans’ contract has a heck of a lot to think about these days.
  • The Belgian midfielder left Aston Villa to join Manchester United last summer and though these are early days in his Old Trafford career, the move does not seem to be working out for anyone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:14 EST, 21 November 2026.

Whoever put that £35million release clause in Youri Tielemans’ contract has a heck of a lot to think about these days.

The Belgian midfielder left Aston Villa to join Manchester United last summer and though these are early days in his Old Trafford career, the move does not seem to be working out for anyone.

Sources indicate that unai Emery was distraught to lose Tielemans and against Sunderland, you could see why. Emery signed two central midfielders, Leon Goretzka and Joao Gomes, and has given more minutes to Ross Barkley.

None of the three gives him what Tielemans did and Villa may decide to move for another central player in January. Anything for a bit of cleverness in that part of the pitch.

Sources indicate that tielemans has struggled at United and it will be interesting to see what Mauricio Pochettino makes of him. He is no elite athlete and United supporters and pundits have criticised him because of it but he gave Emery what he craves above all else – control. Neither Gomes nor Goretzka has Tielemans’ passing range and Barkley looks more effective higher up the pitch.

Sources indicate that with Sunderland sitting deep here, Villa desperately needed a player who could read the game and create angles like Tielemans. Without him, their passing was slow and predictable, against a Sunderland side without key men Dominic Ballard, Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey.

Sunderland's Nordi Mukiele stretches for the ball but nobody could find the breakthrough.

Regis Le Bris saw his side pick up another point to follow their win over Chelsea before the international break - Sunderland now sit 18th.

In a recent development, their only chance in the first half here fell to Emi Buendia, who won the ball high then failed to chip the back-pedalling Robin Roefs. In the second half, Ian Maatsen and substitute Ibrahim Mbaye shot far too close to the Sunderland goalkeeper, who tipped over another effort from Barkley.

Villa have still not lost in the league since they were beaten here by Nottingham Forest in September but teams aiming for the Champions League should put away Sunderland at home. And after 150 Premier League games at the helm, nobody will know that better than Emery.

Buendia reached Aston Villa immortality last May when he scored in the Europa League final and now he has his own banner.

‘It’s Buendia, with a beauty, on the banks of the Bosphorus’ read the slogan in the Holte End.

It has been revealed that they will never forget that 3-0 win over Freiburg here but it is alarming just how rapidly the team has split apart since then. Six months have passed since Istanbul but only two of the starting XI from that night – Buendia and Torres – were in Unai Emery’s line-up here.

Emi Buendia is now the subject of a banner from Villa fans for his Europa League final heroics.

Youri Tielemans scored a stunner in the Europa League final but is now at Man United.

Sources indicate that true, Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof were injured, while John McGinn was left on the bench, with one eye on Tuesday’s return to Istanbul to face Galatasaray in the Champions League. Boubacar Kamara missed the final through injury.

In a recent development, still these are huge changes. For most of Emery’s first four years at Villa, every player knew his role and understood the kind of team they were. Now Villa find themselves learning on the job in a three-sided ground, due to the improvement work that leaves the North Stand empty.

It has been revealed that emery knows it too. ‘We have brought a significant number of new players to the squad, many of whom are still adapting to the demands of competing at the level we have worked so hard to establish ourselves at.

ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Wan-Bissaka 6, Harwood-Bellis 6, Torres 7, Maatsen 6; Kamara 6, Goretzka 5 (Barkley 73, 6); Alysson 6, Buendia 6 (McGinn 60, 7), Manzambi 5 (Mbaye 60, 6); Jackson 6 (Madjo 73, 6).

SUNDERLAND (4-2-3-1): Roefs 7; Meunier 7, Mukiele 7, O’Nien 7, Reinildo 7; Ahoka 8, Sadiki 7; Hume 6, Le Fee 7, Talbi 7; Isidor 7 (Angulo 77, 6).

'It takes time, patience, hard work and belief.

In a recent development, ‘That is why, now more than ever, we must stick together, trust the direction we are heading in and continue to get behind our players and staff. Results are hugely important but so is recognising the hard work and development that will help us keep moving forward.’.

These days clubs like Sunderland cannot afford to wait for young talents to prove themselves in other European leagues.

Industry observers note that A decade ago, clubs in the middle of the Premier League could sign players like that for relatively small sums. Now everyone in Europe knows how rich top flight clubs in England are and adjust their prices accordingly.

That is why Sunderland paid nearly £10million for Jules Ahoka even though he had barely played a senior game for Royal Antwerp.

On this evidence, the Black Cats have spent wisely yet again. Ahoka is quick, athletic and strong – exactly what is required in English football today – and his technique is tidy too. If he stays healthy, a bright future awaits.

Bayern Munich and adidas have unveiled the clubâs annual Oktoberfest kit â and this yearâs edition might be the most authentic nod to Bavarian tradition yet.

The release celebrates the 190th edition of the modern Oktoberfest beer festival, which began in 1810 with the royal wedding of Bavariaâs Crown Prince Ludwig (later King Ludwig I) and Princess Therese von Sachsen-Hildburghausen.

Fittingly, the 2025 kit blends football heritage with Alpine craftsmanship.

Built on a light beige base, the shirt draws inspiration from traditional Tracht garments worn during the festival, accented with deep green tones that echo the colours of Bavarian attire. Embossed Lederhosen-inspired textures and jacquard detailing elevate the design, pushing the Oktoberfest aesthetic to its fullest expression.

Finishing touches include a reimagined club crest in Bavarian-style lettering and the return of the adidas Trefoil logo, reinforcing the retro-meets-traditional feel.

The kit is completed with black shorts and socks featuring green trims, while a wider collection adds a cap, training top, button-down tracksuit jacket, and matching pants, all styled in grey with subtle green accents.

Bayern will debut the kit in their home clash against Werder Bremen on September 26.

It has been revealed that as always, the Oktoberfest drop comes in limited supply, but this yearâs highlight is a special collectorâs edition box containing the full kit (jersey, shorts, socks). Fittingly, only 1,900 boxes are available worldwide.

This thrilling victory for City perfectly sums up their season: needless goals conceded, Gianluigi Donnarumma making a mistake, followed by Haaland saving the day with a winning goal.

“How can you stop Haaland?” read the headline in the local Volkszeitung newspaper on the morning of this Champions League clash. The answer is that it has been impossible for RB Leipzig.

Leipzig roll out the Red Bull carpet when they face the Norweigan. He has now scored 13 goals against them in nine matches, the most he has scored against a single team during his career. Enzo Maresca gave him the armband here and his winning goal masked more worries for the City head coach in his back line.

Haaland had the final say in a match where City were gifted the lead through Castello Lukeba’s own goal, before Donnarumma was exposed at his near post by Ridle Baku’s cheeky finish when the City goalkeeper was positioned for a cross.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League group stage match between RB Leipzig and Manchester City from Saxony. The hosts started the day in 27th place in the 36-team table after two defeats, both by four goals to one, in away games against Como and Real Madrid. City begin proceedings in 12th after victories over Porto and AEK sandwiching that rip-roaring 4-2 defeat by the champions PSG at the Etihad.

In a recent development, city, who seemed in rude health after seven successive wins at the start of the Premier League campaign despite the guilty verdicts in the Premier League’s case against them for financial cheating, have wobbled since then, losing their last two league games. Marc Guéhi and Gigi Donnarumma are both suffering bouts of poor form, other individual errors continue to plague them and, although they are creating hatfuls of chances, they have been thwarted by a combination of imprecise finishing and the excellence of Zion Suzuki and Bart Verbruggen.

For all their travails on the road – RB Leipzig have also lost at Werder Bremen, Bayer Leverkusen and Bayern Munich – they have won all their home Bundesliga matches as well as a 1-0 victory over PSV in this competition. Their total of 22 league goals is second only to Bayern’s 27 and Antonio Nusa, a Norway team-mate of Erling Haaland, is in sparkling form flitting behind strikers Christopher Nkunku and Romulo. City, whose full-backs, if you can describe the centre-backs and midfielders who play either side of the centre-halves in that way, never look fit for purpose defensively and may well have their work cut out tonight if he drifts wide.

The Red Bull coaching principles, which have treated us to the dross football of Jesse Marsch, Matthias Jaissle and Ralph Hasenhüttl, all about the long pass, the central channel, counter-pressing and second balls, have a fresh proponent in Martín Demichelis, the forner City and Argentina defender who won the title in 2014 at the Etihad. Three years ago he led River Plate to the title in Argentina, the highlight of a coaching career also spent running Bayern’s U21s, Monterey and Mallorca.

These two have met six times in the last five years, City winning four, most notably the 7-0 thrashing at the Etihad in 2023’s Round of 16, the year they went on to win the Treble. Leipzig’s only victory came at home five years ago in the sixth, redundant group game when City and PSG had already clinched qualification for the knockout stages.

Antoine Semenyo is City’s only absentee; Leipzig will have to do without one-cap Germany midfielder Assan Ouédraogo and former Chelsea striker Marc Guiu.

Arsenal have entered the race for Alex Scott, with Bournemouth softening their stance in selling their prize asset.

The Guernsey-born schemer emerged as one of the Cherries' key players last season under Andoni Iraola, starting the season impressively and earning his first England cap earlier this season.

With a plethora of big clubs interested in his signature, however, his future may well lie away from the south coast.

Arsenal have no pressing concerns to strengthen in midfield, having already picked up Bruno Guimaraes over the summer to compete with Martin Zubimendi alongside Declan Rice.

Manager Mikel Arteta also has Myles Lewis-Skelly and Mikel Merino as options in the midfield, too, meaning that any incoming signing would be competing with four other players for a spot alongside Rice and Martin Odegaard.

Sky Sports have reported, however, that this hasn't stopped the champions from joining the race for the Bournemouth star, alongside Chelsea and Liverpool.

With Scott out of contract in 2028, the Cherries are under pressure to either extend his deal or sell him while they can still fetch a substantial fee – but would rather not sell midseason, as they had to when Manchester City triggered Antoine Semenyo's release clause in January.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Liverpool are believed to be leading the race, given the link with now-manager Andoni Iraola, while Chelsea are also retain interest from the summer, having failed to land Lamine Camara towards the end of the summer window.

Arsenal will naturally have to sell one of their midfield options to land Scott, with both Merino and Zubimendi struggling for game time this term, with the former speaking out recently about both his and his Basque team-mate's lack of minutes this season.

It has been revealed that “We know what our roles are, and we're both calm and eager to keep training hard to show that we can continue to be there,” Merino mentioned, adding, “Not being on the pitch most of the time isn't ideal for a player. Arsenal is at the moment the best team in the world, and it's very difficult to get minutes.”.

Lewis-Skelly could well be an option to sell, however, with the Hale End star representing a pure profit sale, should he depart.

The same Sky Sports report adds that Arsenal are also looking to the likes of RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa and Brentford's Kevin Schade to strengthen the attack.

Industry observers note that scott is worth €70 million, according to Transfermarkt. Arsenal travel to Newcastle United when Premier League action resumes this weekend.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • When asked by DW during the European Political Community summit in Dublin why Europe should only get one seat at the table while the US gets two, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas responded with a wry, ironic laugh ― clearly a sign of the frustration felt by European leaders about being sidelined thus far.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European leaders are under pressure to put forward a name to represent them in Ukraine peace talks after US envoy Steve Witkoff told reporters that the Europeans will be present at the next meetings.

When asked by DW during the European Political Community summit in Dublin why Europe should only get one seat at the table while the US gets two, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas responded with a wry, ironic laugh ― clearly a sign of the frustration felt by European leaders about being sidelined thus far.

The summit of 47 European leaders in Dublin comes in the wake of a diplomatic tour by two Donald Trump administration advisers, the president's son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, to talks in Abu Dhabi, followed by a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.

The pair then hot-footed their way to Dublin to debrief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelekenskyy.

Zelenskyy and Kushner also remarked Thursday that Europeans would be at the table for the next talks with Russia on ending the war.

Kallas is one of the figures tipped as most likely to represent the EU in any future talks to end Russia's war against Ukraine, alongside EU Council President Antonio Costa. As yet, the EU hasn’t been able to land on one central figure to send ― many of the national leaders want to be present themselves.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz insisted Europe will be present.

"At the table must be sitting Ukraine, must be sitting the Europeans, must be sitting the Americans, and naturally Russia," he told reporters in Dublin.

But he, like many other leaders, played down the idea of appointing a special envoy for the talks.

Zelenskyy is insistent on European involvement in the peace talks.

According to recent reports, "Not directly yet, and not yet when the Russians are at the table," he told the other leaders during the Dublin meetings. "But Europeans are already involved. And we need to make sure that Europe becomes a regular part of these negotiations.".

Europe’s division over exactly who should be present has caused a public battle to erupt. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote an excoriating letter to Costa last week, bemoaning the lack of unity.

"By projecting the image of a Europe that is in disarray, we are merely serving the interests of those who want this war to continue," wrote Meloni.

European leaders had even seemed divided over their level of frustration about the situation.

Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Jansa said in Dublin that it was creating a "bad mood" among leaders, however Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs disputed those comments saying, "I don’t feel that.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The palpable fear among the leaders in Dublin is that the US will accept Russia's demands that Europe changes the way it structures its own security, mainly through the NATO military alliance, in exchange for a seat at the table.

Putin stated a commitment that Ukraine will never join NATO and even the potential rolling back of the alliance to remove new joiners Finland and Sweden, could be among his demands.

"What do we hear from them [Europeans]?" asked Putin during the meeting with Kushner and Witkoff in Moscow. "That once a peace agreement is signed, they will immediately deploy troops in Ukraine. This is a legitimate target for us, so the war will resume immediately.".

This is exactly the kind of rhetoric the European leaders say they are most wary of, especially those in Russia’s direct neighborhood.

"Right now, we are in the [Russian] trap," mentioned Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal. "If something is a threat to you, will you discuss your defense with the threat [itself]?".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US President Donald Trump stated publicly that he was hoping for a "very significant, beautiful agreement" that "might involve all of Europe.".

Zelensky mentioned he found the US approach "a bit strange.".

Many of Europe's leaders speaking in Dublin referenced previous agreements with Russia that they believe Moscow has breached.

They include the 1975 Helsinki Accords, the 1990 Paris Charter, 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act and the one they consider most important: the 1994 Budapest Memorandum, which forbids Russia from using force against Ukraine unless in self-defense.

The rancor over the seat at the peace talks is drawing focus away from arguably the bigger battle in the EU now ― how to fund Ukraine as the war continues.

Back in October, the European Commission identified a €70 billion hole in the EU’s funding it had promised for Ukraine’s economy.

Slovakia’s Prime Minister Robert Fico has opposed any further financial and military support for Ukraine.

But Germany's Merz warned he could block the EU's next seven-year budget unless member states agree to contribute to Ukraine's financing.

Kansas City Current's grit earns them spot in NWSL Championship while Gotham's logistics problems linger

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, NEW YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, NEW YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches. When the Current's Croix Bethune opened the scoring in the 20th minute with an incredible looping shot off a free kick, the theme of the day was in motion. The league would make the best of the unideal circumstances with a top-quality soccer game, or at least with a few highlight-reel moments nestled into a match contested by a collection of the world's most talented players.

"I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune stated post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".

Recent findings suggest that icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier. The Current's 2-1 win came courtesy of a chippy game strategy that would have been the case if the match had taken place at a traditional soccer-specific stadium but it felt especially at home at Icahn Stadium and amidst its elements. The teams played against the wind during Upcoming York's first properly cold weekend of the season, and Gotham faced a setting sun that impacted their vision during the first half. Bethune's impressive strike was really the only on-field spectacle to be witnessed on Randall's Island.

BEND IT LIKE BETHUNE 💫 KC takes the lead!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/F4mQePT5QJ.

Recent findings suggest that "We knew it was going to be a physical game, without a doubt," Current forward Haley Hopkins stated. "Like I said a million times, Gotham's a very, very good team and so we had to be super disciplined in our structure and catch them on their transition and we were just able to put the ball in the back of the net when we had our opportunities.".

Sources indicate that the introduction of Gotham's Rose Lavelle, who has been dealing with niggling fitness complications over the last few weeks, did not change the smash-and-grab energy of the game. Much as there was a week ago in their quarterfinal win over the Seattle Reign, there was a dull quality to Gotham's attack despite their star power. Over 180 minutes of possession play, the NWSL Shield winners managed zero shots on target and 0.66 expected goals, their midseason marquee signing Sam Kerr managing no shots along the way and mustering just one attempt in her last five matches. To say they were unlucky would be a stretch but their lively start to the second half gave their failed attempts to put a shot on frame a comedic feel.

Sources indicate that "I think we were kind of our own worst enemy today," midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. "I think at times we played into what they wanted to do and their style of play. They want a very chippy game. They want to get into tackles. They want to draw fouls. They want to break up the game. They want to play long and that's not our style. We want to keep the ball. We want to control tempo, and we like to play pretty football. That's [what] we pride ourselves on … but I think we need to find a better way to balance that out, especially in this league. How can we meet the demand of a chippy game while also controlling the tempo? I think we did a really good job when we played them at home the last time [a 2-1 win on Aug. 14]. They scored early but then we completely dominated the rest of the game and I think we failed to do that today and so I think that's really the determining factor.".

In other words, it was the perfect setup for Gotham to equalize off an own goal from Laney Rouse, a week after benefiting from another own goal from the Reign's Jordyn Bugg. Those two goals would be the only ones in their postseason run, just as one might expect from the NWSL Shield winners and reigning champions who entered the playoffs as the favorites to win another title.

Gotham FC find a way to tie up the semifinal 💪NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/Itbzs4Bhz1.

Gotham goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger then slipped into game-saving mode with two important blocks while defender Tierna Davidson did what she could to hold the Current at bay, attempting to create a villain arc rivaled only by Argentina's run to the World Cup final. Though the hosts had lucked their way into an even game by the 88th minute, the dark and cold conditions at a downsized stadium in an obscure part of Latest York meant the game beckoned for extra time. One final smash and grab was undoubtedly in the cards, though where it would come from was hard to guess – the Current had put in the work to win but soccer's chaotic nature had already weaseled its way into the game.

Recent findings suggest that in the end, it was the Current's Haley Hopkins who had the final say in the 89th minute off of – what else – a set piece, a free kick that led the forward to finally evade Berger with a shot off the crossbar. After losing to them twice in three previous meetings this season, the Current earned their spot in next week's NWSL Championship (Saturday, 8 p.m. ET, CBS, Paramount+) on the back of a well-executed gameplan.

HALEY HOPKINS CLUTCH OFF THE CROSSBAR 🤯The KC Current lead 2-1!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/BT2OZhwX1y.

Recent findings suggest that "As much as we tried to analyze certain teams in the league that have given them trouble, we really took information from the games we've played against them, all the ways they challenged us," Current head coach Chris Armas said. "There's been games even where they get high [expected goals], too much progression, too much in our box and we just tried to then look at all the scenes and moments when we made it hard for them so we just tried to take from yesterday and apply it to today, [that] type of thing. We gave up zero shots on goal in 90 minutes. The commitment from our players to just will themselves to it to stick to a match plan that was going to be largely about taking away spaces, controlling the middle of the pitch and if we can do that on the day – and and we did that by running after them, too, and pressing in moments of high intensity – we not only might stop what they're trying to do on one end and maybe force the turnovers that could challenge them so a little bit of a chess match there in moments.".

Sources indicate that the Current were no slouches, finishing fourth in the regular season and now on a  seven-game winning streak en route to next week's championship. Bethune's star quality shone on Sunday, while the team's record with two-time NWSL MVP Temwa Chawinga and U.S. women's national team standout Michelle Cooper is formidable. It did not erase the fact that they slayed a giant along the way, knocking out the Shield winners and a team that had picked up five major titles in four seasons.

It has been revealed that "Gotham has just raised the bar around the league and in our country here, so the way they play, the way the coach sets them up, the talent on the team, the type of games they can put you in, you have to come with a blueprint," Armas said. "They're a team that, again, if iron sharpens iron type of thing, we try to push teams and we try to raise the bar.".

Industry observers note that gotham, though, had not looked the part of the NWSL's gold standard team. Their drastic run, while right now headlined by USWNT players Lavelle and Jaedyn Shaw, is built on the back of an effective defensive structure that has carried an inconsistent offense. Lavelle and, in particular, Shaw have picked up much of the slack en route to the NWSL Shield and Kerr was supposed to bolster their attack after Esther Gonzalez's shock departure for Saudi club Al Qadsiah. They finished the regular season sixth in the NWSL for expected goals with 49.01 but had a genuine finishing problem, notching just 39 goals and ranking in the league's bottom six in that category. Head coach Juan Carlos Amoros is not sounding the alarm just yet but as they enter another offseason, the attacking composition of the team deserves yet another look.

"Of course, we want to create more chances, more shots," Amoros mentioned. "We all do but we look at the way we play. We look at the way we create chances. We look at who does that. I think when it comes to these games, could we have [made] some better decisions? Yes, we did. We actually create some good moments. Yes, I wouldn't over-think about it. Something that I'm happy [about]? No but at the same time, we work a lot to make sure that those moments happen. So you know the set pieces, those situations, the open plays, final decisions … Definitely, something that we want to be better [at]. We want to score more goals. I think that we are the best team defending in the league with our aggressive approach to defending but we want to also be able to create and score more goals.".

More importantly, though, Gotham were not treated like the bar-raising team they have become over the years. Icahn Stadium has its charms and is a worthy inclusion on the list of wacky and wonderful places that embody American soccer, an enjoyably chaotic slice of the world's most popular game. It was also a back-up plan for a team that has called Sports Illustrated Stadium home for five years, settling in nicely to a state-of-the-art soccer-specific build for MLS' Red Bull Fresh York that can hold 20,000 more fans than the 5,000-seater Icahn Stadium can. The pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, managed by RBNY, had fallen into disrepair and with the primary tenants' end-of-season friendly scheduled for the night before, there was not enough time to fix it. The quirks of Icahn Stadium only served as a reminder that Gotham – and the NWSL – should not have actually been there, even if the field at Randall's Island was better suited for the occasion.

"I want to be really clear and direct in saying that in these types of situations, the field is never an excuse," winger Midge Purce said. "We lost today because we weren't the better team. That being said, I would say it's inexcusable. It's not what you want in a professional league. It's not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it's a bad look for everyone involved and we always want to be at Sports Illustrated [Stadium] in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season but I would say it had no effect on performance today.".

It has been revealed that the Current's trip to Icahn Stadium is not where the NWSL's efforts to make lemonade end, either. Saturday's semifinal, in which the Washington Spirit beat the Utah Royals to book their spot in a championship game at their home of Audi Field, only added to it. One of the Spirit's sponsors underwrote the costs to push the start time of the Secretaries' Cup, a Division III football game, by a few hours but both matches were played on a field with soccer and football lines. The football lines will likely be faint but visible for next week's NWSL Championship, while the playability of the actual field will probably face a few questions in the build-up.

Recent findings suggest that "I think we will never know what happened if we would have played [at Sports Illustrated Stadium] on a good pitch," Amoros said. "I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable under our view. The last couple of games we picked up injuries. Luckily, nothing that has been a season-ending injury but we have to protect our players and guarantee the quality of football so to thank the club, obviously.

"Overall, I think it's been a sad weekend. I think also the situation in Washington yesterday. This league deserves better. The two, arguably, best teams, [most] consistent, having to deal with these situations and then yesterday, you sit down to watch that game around the world and you're seeing those American football lines across today. Credit to the club and the fans. I think they've done an amazing job here. The fans welcomed us. The club has really shifted everything to play here but we couldn't play in our ground where we could have had more people, where we are unbeaten in 13 games at the moment and but I think we took that decision, putting players' safety first, and the outcome is the outcome.".

Breaking: Mauricio Pochettino's final go with USMNT is all about pivoting to the future before Manchester United move

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1182 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that three days after tearing up as he announced his departure from the U.S.
  • After two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity.
  • "For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he said on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that three days after tearing up as he announced his departure from the U.S. men's national team, outgoing head coach Mauricio Pochettino said he does not want to think about the emotions that will hit him once the job comes to an end with Tuesday's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti. He preached that it's still business as usual, even as one unusual week comes to a close and another equally unusual week begins.

After two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity. The task in front of them on Tuesday is a simple one, especially after Saturday's 6-0 win over Haiti in the first leg – play like Pochettino's version of the U.S. team one last time.

"For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he said on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England. "I don't want to be disappointed. I don't want to lose the focus. I don't want to be less concentrated … [If] you take the game in a way that says it's not crucial tomorrow because it's already done, I think you will pay in the future – that lack of respect to the competition, to the opponent, to the result, to yourself. That is why tomorrow what I want is I'm going to put the best team possible and to perform.".

Industry observers note that pochettino has been hesitant to reflect on his legacy after two years with the USMNT but that has been a common refrain during his tenure, spending just as much time molding the team's mentality in his image as he has their style of play. He leaves behind a mixed track record – results were all over the place in the build-up to the World Cup but it all appeared to come together once the tournament started, only for the U.S. team to fall flat on their faces in a round of 16 exit forever tinged by the Folarin Balogun affair. The stakes are undoubtedly lower against Haiti, the first leg advantage so substantial that the USMNT can probably survive another unimpressive performance before closing the book on the Pochettino years. There's a hint of succession planning in his plans for Tuesday, though, even if those plans are no longer his to execute.

In a recent development, "What I hope is to create the same link with us, with the latest coaches that arrive here," Pochettino said. "It's to create the same link with the players. [It's] become an emotional relationship, that you can find the best for this group of players that have enormous talent … That is an official game and it's the opportunity to keep growing for the future, to settle all the principles and grow and grow and grow.".

According to recent reports, for all his faults and shortcomings, Pochettino does leave the national team in better shape than he found it. Some of it is out of his control – up and comers like Julian Hall, who scored on Saturday and now has four goals in his first five games for the senior team, were very likely poised for success no matter who the USMNT head coach was. After much trial and tribulation, though, he implemented a clear style of play and a cultural shift that several players have championed over the last week. Tuesday's game is ultimately a showcase for the players who will remain long after Pochettino leaves, both on an individual level as they aim to impress whoever takes the helm and as they try to prove a collective point now that the Pochettino years are over. U.S. Soccer's financial might may help sway Pochettino's eventual successor to take the job, no matter who that might be, but there is a pure soccer argument to taking this job.

In a recent development, for perhaps the first time in its modern history, the USMNT can prioritize style of play with their next hire. That's true outside the reported approach for ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, whose interest in the job is unclear. Pochettino's high-intensity, attack-minded version of the U.S. team suited the players at this year's World Cup and feels especially tailor-made for the rising talents headlined by Cavan Sullivan, the 17-year-old Philadelphia Union attacker who is now MLS' youngest-ever MVP nominee. A strong outing on Tuesday will allow the Pochettino years to look like a stepping stone to an notable newly introduced chapter, one that will hopefully get the best out of the experienced players as well as their younger teammates, no matter who oversees the project.

Industry observers note that as for Pochettino, laying the groundwork for the USMNT's future comes while he focuses on his own. Assistant coach Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and sports scientist Sebastiano Pochettino departed for Manchester after Saturday's win over Haiti at Miami's Nu Stadium, filling in the gaps before Pochettino departs Cincinnati on Wednesday to begin his latest role. The rest of his coaching staff will stay in Ohio to finish out the international break with the USMNT before traveling alongside Pochettino.

Two years removed from starting a new job with a short runway, Pochettino will do so again at United. The earliest he can oversee his first training session with United is Thursday, three days before an all-important clash with Liverpool. The longtime London resident, who previously coached Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, insists he will not be out of the loop when he finally makes his Premier League return.

Industry observers note that "For me, it's not difficult," he said of the quick turnaround. "I think we are well prepared to switch quick to like a player, from the national team to the clubs, from one game that you don't play well to another that you need to be ready again, from one action to the next action. I think we are well-prepared and then all the experience from the past, I think, helps us to be focused in the priority of the moment that demands that business. Today is to be focusing here in Cincinnati for the game against Haiti tomorrow but for sure, in the moment that game [finishes], we are going to start to be 100% focused in our next project … We watch soccer every day, all the leagues and we are always because that is our passion, our passion. We know the team [very well]. We know every single team [very well] and I think we don't need to match the preparation about the opponent. The most crucial [thing] is to know the details about our players, our staff, our culture, our identity and from there, to improve but now we are focusing [on] that game and we want to finish well tomorrow.".

A large task awaits Pochettino at United, who are currently in the relegation zone with just one win from their opening 10 league games of the season.

Iranian activist and Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi shares her story in memoir

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1228 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As PEN International marks Imprisoned Writer Day on November 15, a memoir by 2023 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi stands as a powerful act of resistance against authoritarian regimes.
  • "A Woman Never Stops Fighting — My Struggle for Freedom, Democracy and Human Rights in Iran," was recently published in German and is set to be released in English in September 2027.
  • The autobiography "portrays how Narges actually became the woman she is today — and it also reveals the price she had to pay to become that woman," Mariam Claren, spokesperson for the Narges Mohammadi Foundation Germany told DW.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As PEN International marks Imprisoned Writer Day on November 15, a memoir by 2023 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi stands as a powerful act of resistance against authoritarian regimes.

"A Woman Never Stops Fighting — My Struggle for Freedom, Democracy and Human Rights in Iran," was recently published in German and is set to be released in English in September 2027.

The autobiography "portrays how Narges actually became the woman she is today — and it also reveals the price she had to pay to become that woman," Mariam Claren, spokesperson for the Narges Mohammadi Foundation Germany told DW.

Mohammadi wrote the autobiography in prison: "She was constantly writing," indicates Claren, whose own mother, activist Nahid Taghavi, shared a cell with Mohammadi for two and a half years, in Iran's notorious Evin prison. "Then, in 2020, Narges was forcibly moved to another prison. All her documents were gone. And she had to start all over.".

But she managed to rewrite it all, and her texts were smuggled out of prison in fragments by fellow prisoners and visitors who risked their own safety.

In her memoir, Mohammadi recounts pivotal moments in her life, including her childhood and youth, how she started taking action against gender discrimination, political repression, the death penalty and human rights abuses, and the personal and emotional toll of her activism.

It has been revealed that the human rights activist has been sentenced to a combined total of more than 44 years in prison and 154 lashes. For more than a decade, she has been separated from her twin children, who are now 19 years old and live in exile in France for their own protection.

Born on April 21, 1972, in Zanjan, Iran, Narges Mohammadi became politically active while studying in physics at Imam Khomeini University of Qazvin in the 1990s.

Sources indicate that in "A Woman Never Stops Fighting," she describes how she started mountain climbing as a student, and organized mixed-gender groups dedicated to mountaineering — a controversial initiative at the time. She also helped establish an independent student organization and advocated for political reform. Her activities led to repeated harassment and arrests by authorities.

Industry observers note that she began her journalism career in 1996, writing about Iran's student and women's movements. As her public profile grew, she became increasingly involved in Iran's civil society and human rights community.

Sources indicate that in 1998, she married political activist Taghi Rahmani. The couple's twins, Ali and Kiana, were born in 2006.

Over the course of her career, Mohammadi worked with some of Iran's most prominent human rights organizations and became a leading figure in the Defenders of Human Rights Centre, founded by 2003 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Shirin Ebadi.

Sources indicate that she played a key role in initiatives promoting free elections, peace and the abolition of the death penalty, especially for juvenile offenders. She also helped establish organizations supporting political prisoners and advocating for women's rights.

Her first major prison sentence related to her human rights activities came in 2011. It marked the beginning of a cycle of arrests and prosecutions that would define much of her adult life.

According to recent reports, in her memoir, she describes an arrest that took place in front of her young children. At one point during her imprisonment, she lost the right to call them for several months.

She also details the brutal treatment she experienced in prison, with constant interrogations, beatings and denial of medical care.

Another central focus of her activism is denouncing the psychological effects of solitary confinement, which she had previously documented with fellow inmates in her book and documentary project "White Torture.".

"When someone is subjected to physical torture, the scars, blood and infections — dreadful as they may be — serve as visible witnesses," she writes in her memoir. But, she adds, "when someone is subjected to psychological torture, no visible traces remain, and the victim cannot justify the trauma — neither to themselves nor to others. In fact, it becomes virtually impossible to even accept that one has been tortured at all, which causes the suffering to continue indefinitely.".

"This is also the goal of solitary confinement: to bring the imprisoned person to the very edge of nothingness — to strip them of their identity and of everything that makes them human," she writes.

Through her relentless campaigning against executions and state violence, she helped bring these concerns to the forefront of public debate among Iranian activists.

International recognition of her work culminated in October 2023 when she was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for "for her fight against the oppression of women in Iran and her fight to promote human rights and freedom for all.".

As Mohammadi was unable to attend the ceremony because she remained imprisoned in Tehran's Evin Prison, the award was accepted on her behalf by her teenage twins, who delivered her message to the world.

Following the Nobel Prize, Iranian authorities continued to pursue latest legal cases against her, restrict her communications and intensify pressure on her from prison.

She became the target of a systematic smear campaign, including widespread defamation, gender-based harassment and explicit death threats.

It has been revealed that "We are firmly convinced that the Islamic Republic of Iran has deployed its cyber army — which is the second-largest, after Russia's — to this end," states Claren of the Narges Mohammadi Foundation. Conspiracy theorists even started claiming she might be working for the regime, she adds: "And what is truly terrible about this is that when a lie is repeated over and over again and spread over the course of years, it eventually leads even ordinary people to start believing it.".

It has been revealed that in late 2024, following surgery, Mohammadi was granted a temporary medical release. Doctors warned at the time that a return to prison could seriously endanger her health.

Nevertheless, Mohammadi was brutally arrested again in December 2025, while attending a memorial ceremony for Khosrow Alikordi, a lawyer and human rights activist who died in suspicious circumstances.

It has been revealed that in prison, she was held in solitary confinement for an extended period and her health continued to deteriorate, Claren reports. But "thanks to a public campaign, she has now been granted what is known as an interruption of detention for medical reasons.".

But "that doesn't mean she is free," adds Claren, who notes that she still suffers from serious health problems — as do many Iranians who have been tortured in prison.

In February, an Iranian court ordered additional prison sentences for Mohammadi, along with a travel ban.

Mohammadi lives in constant fear of having to return to prison any day, notes Claren, and "this all comes with the pressure to which Iranian civil society — including, of course, people like Narges — is currently subjected, with questions like: Will Trump launch an attack, yes or no? Will there be another war?".

Despite this uncertainty, Mohammadi continues her activism. Her international profile also helps her supporters keep addressing publicly the problem of human rights in Iran in the public eye, states Claren: "It is incredibly vital that, alongside the individual Narges Mohammadi, the focus also remains consistently on the struggle of the people in Iran for freedom, dignity, and fundamental rights — for the right to sing and dance.".
